description:
There are many things I love about pumpkin pie - the creamy spiced filling, the signal that Autumn is well and truly upon us and the happy notion that I’m sneaking some veggies into my dessert. Things I’m not always such a fan of however, include: waiting for the pastry to rest, the faff of lining a tart tin and having to convince the made-up minds of friends and family members with previous bad pumpkin pie experiences that it can be in fact, delicious.One look and bite of these simple, stress-free, pumpkin pie bars with a press-in pecan crust will sway any pumpkin pie sceptics within an instant. They are deceptively good, taste even better the next day and they just so happen to be plant based, as well as low FODMAP, for any eaters that need them to be. A bonus element: the crust to filling ratio is almost 50/50, which for pumpkin pie is how I like it and think you might too.Feel free to sub in dairy butter and lactose free milk and if you don’t have a strong blender to help blitz the pecans, you can use ground almonds instead.

notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 1 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~383 g x 1 = 383 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~41 g (inferred ~10.73% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.

name: ✅ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Katsu Curry – Tofu Katsu Curry with Carrot & Radish Pickle
ingredients:
260 g [recipe:ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Katsu Curry Sauce]
1 200g Block of extra-firm tofu, drained and pressed
50g Dried gluten free breadcrumbs
1 Tbsp cornflour
Sea salt and freshly ground black pepper
Vegetable oil, for frying
For the carrot and radish pickle:
2 Medium carrots
1 Small bunch of radishes
2 Tbsp White wine vinegar
1 Tsp Caster sugar
Sea salt and black pepper
To serve :
Fluffy White rice
2-3 Spring onions, green tops only, finely sliced  🟢 Fructose 20% (15 g per serving)
Small bunch of coriander
directions:
1. Make the home-made sauce first, [recipe:ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Katsu Curry Sauce], or use a frozen portion.

2. To make the carrot and radish pickle, toss all of the ingredients together in a bowl and allow to marinate for 15 minutes. Drain and set aside until ready to serve.

3. To prepare the tofu, slice the block into two rectangular pieces and pat off any excess moisture. Add the cornflour to a small bowl and combine with 4 tablespoons of boiling water. Allow to sit for a few minutes until it thickens. Meanwhile, add the breadcrumbs to another bowl and season generously with salt and pepper.

4. Coat the tofu in the cornflour mix, followed by the seasoned breadcrumbs, using your hands to encourage the breadcrumbs to stick. Repeat the process again, placing the breaded tofu in the cornflour mix and then the breadcrumbs once more.

5. Heat a shallow layer of oil in a frying pan and when hot, add the breaded tofu. Cook on a medium-low heat for 5-6 minutes on each side, or until crisp and golden on the outside and piping hot throughout. Make sure the oil’s not so hot that it burns the breadcrumbs before the tofu is cooked. Remove the tofu from the pan and let rest on some kitchen paper.

6. Empty the Stir-in Katsu Curry Sauce into a saucepan and place over a medium heat. Simmer for a couple of minutes until piping hot.

7. To serve, plate up rice and a few spoonfuls of the pickle. Slice the tofu in strips diagonally and place on top of the rice. Drizzle over the katsu sauce, sprinkle some spring onion and scatter over some coriander. Recipe created by Cook and Author Emma Hatcher (www.shecanteatwhat.com).
notes:

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Teriyaki – Teriyaki Vegetable Stir-Fry
ingredients:
260 g [recipe:✅ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Teriyaki Sauce]
300g Straight to wok gluten free noodles or microwaveable rice (about)
280g Firm tofu, cubed  🟠 Galacto-oligosaccharides 82% (140 g per serving)
90g Edamame  🟡 Galacto-oligosaccharides 60% (45 g per serving)
75g Baby corn
58g Broccoli heads or broccolini heads*  🟢 Fructose 39% (29 g per serving)
34g Mangetout
28g Sugar snap peas
1 Tbsp Cornflour
1 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
1/2 tsp toasted sesame oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (1%)
Garnish with fresh chives and sesame seeds**
directions:
1. Make the home-made sauce first, [recipe:✅ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Teriyaki Sauce], or use a frozen portion.

2. Drain the block of firm tofu, pat dry with kitchen towels and slice into 2cm cubes.

3. In a medium mixing bowl, use a balloon whisk to combine 2 tbsp teriyaki sauce with 1 tbsp cornflour and 1 tbsp olive oil until a thick paste is formed.

4. Pour in the tofu and massage with your hands to coat well. Transfer to a non-stick frying pan or wok and saute on a high heat for 10 minutes, turning with a pair of tongs constantly, until the tofu is golden and crispy. Now set aside in a small bowl.

5. Halve the sugar snap peas and mangetout, halve the baby corn lengthways, remove the stalks from the broccoli and halve, measure out the edamame from a frozen packet.

6. Place 1 tbsp oil of your choice into the pan and bring to a high heat. Add the sugar snaps, mangetout, baby corn and broccoli to saute for 3-5 minutes, turning constantly. Pour in the remaining teriyaki sauce from the jar of Bay’s Kitchen Teriyaki Stir-in Sauce.

7. Stir through the edamame and add in your straight to wok noodles or microwaveable rice pouch. Continue to saute for a further 2 minutes as the noodles and edamame heat.

8. Finally, stir through the tofu and allow it to heat for a minute or so, then divide into portions. Garnish with fresh chopped chives and a sprinkling of sesame seeds and enjoy immediately. Recipe created by Katya from @positivelychronictravels & @katyakozarycontentcreation.

name: ✅ ♡ Sauce - Teriyaki Sauce
ingredients:
1/8 cup water
0.03 cup gluten-free tamari
1 1/8 tsp pure maple syrup (or packed brown sugar)
3/4 tsp rice vinegar
3/8 tsp freshly grated ginger (from a 1-inch knob)
1/8 tsp toasted sesame oil ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (0%)

3/4 tsp cold water (for the slurry)
3/8 tsp thinly sliced spring onion greens, for finishing  🟢 Fructose 1%

1/8 tsp olive oil for a more savory flavor (optional)
directions:
Simmer
1. In a small saucepan, whisk the water, tamari, maple syrup, rice vinegar, grated ginger, and sesame oil.

2. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, then reduce to medium-low. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes so the ginger infuses and the raw vinegar edge softens.

Thicken
3. In a small bowl, stir the cornstarch into 2 tablespoons cold water until smooth with no lumps.

4. Whisk the slurry into the simmering sauce in a slow stream. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, whisking constantly, until glossy and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

5. Pull off the heat. If using, stir in the olive oil.

Finish
6. Taste and adjust: more tamari for salt, more maple for sweetness, a splash more vinegar for brightness.

7. Transfer to a jar or small pitcher. Scatter spring onion greens and sesame seeds over whatever you're saucing right before serving.

name: ✅ ❣ Low FODMAP Beef Stew
ingredients:
3/4 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.5g (2%)
1/2 slices lower sodium bacon, diced
113 g stew meat or boneless beef chuck, cut into 1-inch cubes  💔 Sat fat 5.7g (28%)
1/2 tbsp tomato paste  🟢 Fructans 29%
1/8 cup dry red wine, like Cabernet Sauvignon (or additional low FODMAP broth)
3/4 tsp cornstarch mixed into 1 tbsp cold water (save for the final step, if using an Instant Pot)
1/2 cup low FODMAP broth (I like Fody Foods Vegetable Soup Base)
1/2 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce (or tamari for gluten-free)
1/2 cup quartered baby potatoes
1/8 lb baby carrots
3/4 tsp minced fresh thyme leaves or 1 tsp dried thyme
Salt and pepper
directions:
1. Heat large skillet over medium heat. Add olive oil and bacon. Cook until bacon is crisp. Using tongs, remove the bacon from the skillet and transfer to the slow cooker.

2. To the warm skillet, add the beef cubes. Sear on each side until just browned, about 1 minute per side. Transfer the browned beef and any remaining cooking fat to the slow cooker.

3. To the now-empty skillet, add the tomato paste and red wine. Whisk and gently release any browned bits from the bottom or sides of the pan. Slowly add in the cornstarch slurry, low FODMAP broth, and soy sauce, whisking until smooth. Transfer the liquid to the slow cooker.

4. To the slow cooker, add the baby potatoes, baby carrots, and thyme. Stir to mix. Cook on low for 6-8 hours, high for 4-5 hours, or until the beef and veggies are tender. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

5. Serve warm with optional garnishes.

6. Press the “Saute” setting on the Instant Pot. Once hot, add olive oil and bacon. Cook until the bacon is crisp. Using tongs, remove the bacon from the Instant Pot and set aside.

7. Add the beef cubes to the Instant Pot and sear on each side until just browned, about 1 minute per side. It may help to do this step in batches, using additional cooking oil, as needed, to prevent burning. Using tongs, remove seared beef cubes and set aside.

8. Add the tomato paste and red wine to the Instant Pot. Whisk until smooth while gently scraping the bottom and sides of the Instant Pot to release any of the browned bits. This helps to release flavor, as well as, prevent a “Burn” message from appearing while cooking with the Instant Pot.

9. Cancel the “Saute” setting. Add in the low FODMAP broth, soy sauce, baby potatoes, baby carrots, bacon bits, seared beef cubes, and thyme. Stir to mix.

10. Place the lid on top of the Instant Pot and secure. Set vent to “Sealing”. Select the “Manual” setting on the Instant Pot. Adjust the time to 30 minutes on “High Pressure” and cook. Allow the pressure to naturally release for 10 minutes before carefully switching the vent to “Venting” and releasing any remaining pressure.

11. Prepare the cornstarch slurry and stir into the stew to slightly thicken. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

name: ✅ ❣ Soup - Corn Chowder
ingredients:
1 cup leek, GREEN tops only, thinly sliced
3 spring onions, GREEN tops only, sliced (reserve some for garnish)  🟢 Fructose 12% (9 g per serving)
400 g potato, peeled and diced into 1cm pieces
1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
150 g fresh corn kernels, cut from 2 ears (keeps each serving at or under the 38g cap)
1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water, for a thicker chowder (optional)
Optional garnish: grated cheddar, extra spring onion greens, cracked pepper
2 tbsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.9g (5%)
3 cups water or low-FODMAP chicken broth
1 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.6g (3%)
1/2 cup lactose-free heavy cream  💔 Sat fat 6g (30%)
1/2 tsp salt, plus more to taste
Black pepper, to taste
directions:
**Prep (bowls):**

**Large bowl — aromatics (soften):**
- Thinly slice the leek greens.
- Slice the spring onion greens (reserve some for garnish).

**Large bowl — potato (simmer):**
- Peel and dice the potato.
- Strip the thyme leaves onto this bowl.

**Medium bowl — corn (add later):**
- Cut the corn kernels from the cob.

**Small bowl — slurry (optional):**
- Mix cornstarch with cold water if thickening.

**Medium bowl — finish:**
- Set out reserved spring onion greens, optional grated cheddar and cracked pepper.

**By the hob (no bowl):** olive oil, water or broth, lactose-free milk, cream, salt, pepper.

**1. Soften aromatics bowl:** Heat oil over medium. Soften the aromatics bowl 4–5 minutes without browning.

**2. Potato:** Stir in the potato bowl 1 minute. Add water or broth; simmer covered 12–15 minutes until potato is fork-tender.

**3. Corn:** Stir in the corn bowl; simmer uncovered about 4 minutes. Optionally blend a portion and return for creaminess.

**4. Dairy:** Lower heat; stir in milk and cream. Warm 3–4 minutes without a hard boil. Add slurry if using; simmer 1–2 minutes until coats a spoon.

**5. Finish:** Season with salt and pepper. Serve topped from the finish bowl.

Cool, portion, refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently until piping hot.
notes:
Imported for personal use. Check Monash app for current serve sizes.
Changed (2026-10-14): milk written as low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed), the preferred low FODMAP milks in order (house rule).

name: ✅ ♡ Slow Cooker Low FODMAP Chicken Wild Rice Soup
ingredients:
113 g boneless, skinless chicken breasts  ♥ Sat fat 1.1g (6%)
1/4 cup uncooked wild rice, rinsed and drained
1/4 cup peeled and diced carrots
1/4 tsp dried thyme // note 1
1/4 tsp dried rosemary
1/8 tsp celery seed  🟢 Mannitol 1%
1/2 bay leaves
3/4 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.5g (2%)
1 1/2 cup low FODMAP chicken broth or low FODMAP vegetable broth // note 2
1/2 tbsp cornstarch mixed into ¼ cup cold water (optional)
1/8 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
1/2 tsp fresh lemon juice
Kosher salt and freshly cracked black pepper
Chopped fresh parsley, optional garnish
directions:
**Prep (bowls):**

**Large bowl — chicken:**
- Have the chicken breasts ready.

**Large bowl — grains (slow cook):**
- Rinse and drain the wild rice.

**Medium bowl — veg:**
- Peel and dice the carrots.

**Small bowl — herb mix (optional bloom):**
- Mix the dried thyme, rosemary and celery seed.

**By the hob (no bowl):** olive oil, low FODMAP broth, bay leaves, optional cornstarch slurry, milk, lemon juice, salt, pepper.

**Medium bowl — finish:**
- Chop fresh parsley if using.

**1. Optional bloom:** Warm olive oil in a small skillet; sauté the herb mix 1–2 minutes until fragrant (or skip and add herbs with the oil later).

**2. Slow cook:** Place the chicken, grains, veg, bay leaves and broth in the slow cooker. Add the bloomed herbs (or oil plus herb mix). Cover; cook on low about 6 hours until the chicken is cooked and the rice is tender.

**3. Shred:** Discard the bay leaves. Shred or dice the chicken; set aside briefly.

**4. Finish:** Stir in milk (and optional slurry if thickening). Return the chicken; cook until warmed through (about 15 minutes if using slurry). Stir in lemon juice; adjust salt and pepper. Serve with parsley from the finish bowl.

Cool, portion, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Tikka Masala Sauce
ingredients:
95 g tinned chopped tomatoes  🟢 Fructose 48% (48 g per serving)
80 ml water
30 g light coconut milk  🟢 Sorbitol 25% (15 g per serving)  ♥ Sat fat 1.1g (5%)
1 tbsp tomato purée  🟢 Fructose 12% (7.5 g per serving)
1 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
2 tsp cornflour, mixed with 1 tbsp of the water
4 g fresh coriander (a small handful), chopped
1 1/2 tsp cumin seeds
1/2 tsp caster sugar
2 tsp lemon juice
1 1/2 tsp coriander seeds
2 g fresh ginger (about 1 tsp grated)
1/3 tsp salt
2/3 tsp sweet paprika
1/3 tsp ground turmeric
1 pinch dried chilli flakes
1 pinch ground black pepper
directions:
1. Dry-toast the cumin and coriander seeds in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind.

2. Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat. Add the ginger for 30 seconds, then the ground seeds, paprika, turmeric and chilli and stir for 30-45 seconds, adding a splash of the water if they catch.

3. Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, the rest of the water, sugar and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.

4. Stir in the light coconut milk and the cornflour mixed with water; simmer for 1-2 minutes until thickened.

5. Finish with the lemon juice, fresh coriander and black pepper.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Thai Red Curry Sauce
directions:
1. Dry-toast the cumin seeds for 1 minute, then grind.

2. Blitz or pound the red chillies, lemongrass and ginger with 1 tbsp of the water to a red paste (no oil).

3. Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat and fry the paste with the cumin and cayenne for 2 minutes until fragrant.

4. Add the rest of the water, the light coconut milk, lime leaves, tamari, sugar and salt and bring to a gentle simmer.

5. Add the red pepper and simmer for 4-5 minutes. Stir in the tapioca starch mixed with water and simmer for 1 minute.

6. Finish with the lime juice and coriander; remove the lime leaves.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Tomato & Basil Sauce
directions:
1. Warm the olive oil in a small pan over a medium-low heat (oregano and black pepper don't need frying, so no extra oil).

2. Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, water, balsamic vinegar, oregano, sugar and salt. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.

3. For a thicker sauce, stir in the tapioca starch mixed with water and simmer for 1 minute more (or simmer 10 minutes longer instead).

4. Off the heat, stir in the chives, basil, lemon juice and black pepper. Taste for salt.

5. Cool, then split into single portions, one per serving (about 125 g each). Label with the sauce and date and freeze. Thaw one portion per serving overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Spicy Arrabbiata Sauce
directions:
1. Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat, add the cayenne and chilli flakes and stir for 20-30 seconds (chilli heat is fat-soluble, so this is the step that needs the oil).

2. Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, sundried tomatoes, water, sugar and salt. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until slightly thickened.

3. For a thicker sauce, stir in the tapioca starch mixed with water and simmer for 1 minute more.

4. Finish with the lemon juice and black pepper.

5. Cool, then split into single portions, one per serving (about 120 g each). Label with the sauce and date and freeze. Thaw one portion per serving overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Tikka Masala Sauce
directions:
1. Dry-toast the cumin and coriander seeds in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind.

2. Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat. Add the ginger for 30 seconds, then the ground seeds, paprika, turmeric and chilli and stir for 30-45 seconds, adding a splash of the water if they catch.

3. Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, the rest of the water, sugar and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.

4. Stir in the light coconut milk and the tapioca starch mixed with water; simmer for 1-2 minutes until thickened.

5. Finish with the lemon juice, fresh coriander and black pepper.

6. Cool, then split into single portions, one per serving (about 125 g each). Label with the sauce and date and freeze. Thaw one portion per serving overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Korma Curry Sauce
directions:
1. Dry-toast the coriander and cumin seeds for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind (this replaces the garam masala blend).

2. Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat. Add the ginger for 1 minute, then the ground seeds and turmeric for 30 seconds, adding a splash of water if they catch.

3. Add the tomatoes, water, sugar, salt, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom (these infuse in the liquid, no frying needed). Simmer for 10 minutes, then fish out the cloves and cardamom pods.

4. Stir in the light coconut milk and the tapioca starch mixed with water; simmer gently for 2 minutes until creamy. Do not boil hard.

5. Finish with the lemon juice and black pepper.

6. Cool, then split into single portions, one per serving (about 130 g each). Label with the sauce and date and freeze. Thaw one portion per serving overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Katsu Curry Sauce
directions:
1. Dry-toast the coriander, fenugreek, cumin, fennel and mustard seeds for 1-2 minutes until fragrant (fenugreek turns bitter if it goes past golden), then grind. This replaces the curry powder.

2. Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat. Add the ginger for 30 seconds, then the ground seeds, turmeric and chilli powder for 30 seconds, adding a splash of water if they catch.

3. Add the water, tamari and sugar and simmer for 5 minutes.

4. Stir in the light coconut milk and the tapioca starch mixed with water; simmer for 2 minutes until thick and glossy. For the classic smooth katsu sauce, blend.

5. Finish with the lemon juice and black pepper.

6. Cool, then split into single portions, one per serving (about 135 g each). Label with the sauce and date and freeze. Thaw one portion per serving overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

name: ✅ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Sweet & Sour Sauce
directions:
1. Put the water, pineapple juice, sugar, tomato purée, cider vinegar and salt in a small pan and bring to a simmer. No oil is needed: there are no spices to bloom.

2. Add the peppers and pineapple and simmer for 3-4 minutes until just tender.

3. Stir in the tapioca starch mixed with water and simmer for 1 minute until thick and glossy.

4. Finish with the chives and black pepper.

5. Cool, then split into single portions, one per serving (about 135 g each). Label with the sauce and date and freeze. Thaw one portion per serving overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Thai Massaman Sauce
directions:
1. Dry-toast the coriander and cumin seeds for 1-2 minutes, then grind.

2. Blitz or pound the lemongrass, ginger and coriander stalks with 1 tbsp of the water to a paste (no oil).

3. Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat and fry the paste for 2 minutes, then add the ground seeds, cayenne and turmeric for 30 seconds.

4. Add the rest of the water, cinnamon, cardamom, lime leaves, salt and sugar (these infuse in the liquid). Simmer for 10 minutes; remove the cardamom pods and lime leaves.

5. Stir in the light coconut milk and the tapioca starch mixed with water; simmer gently for 2 minutes. Finish with the lime juice and coriander leaves.

6. Cool, then split into single portions, one per serving (about 125 g each). Label with the sauce and date and freeze. Thaw one portion per serving overnight in the fridge and reheat until piping hot.

ingredients:
150g gluten-free crispy brown or white rice cereal
2 tablespoons ground flax seed
6 tablespoons pumpkin seeds
4 tablespoons sesame seeds, black, white or mix of both
2 tablespoons coconut oil  ❣ Sat fat 3.1g (15%)
200g peanut butter  ❣ Sat fat 2.5g (12%)
125g maple syrup
1 teaspoon flaky sea salt
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
directions:
1. Line an 8″ square baking tin with parchment paper, leaving an overhang on all sides. Mix the cereal, flax seed, pumpkin seeds and sesame seeds in a large bowl to combine.

2. Melt the coconut oil in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Add the peanut butter, maple syrup and salt and stir until warmed through, smooth, and glossy – this will only take a minute or so. Remove from the heat and whisk in the vanilla.

3. Pour the peanut butter maple mixture over cereal mixture and stir thoroughly to coat. Transfer to your prepared pan and press down very firmly (really squish!) to compact. Chill until firm, about an hour.

4. When firm, remove from the tin and cut into 8 bars or 16 squares. These keep best in the fridge for about 4 days.

name: ℹ️ ❣ Cardamom roast rhubarb & 10 minute granola
ingredients:
For the rhubarb:
1 big bunch of rhubarb (around 400g)
50g brown sugar
1/4 teaspoon ground cardamom
For the granola:
4 tablespoons coconut oil  💔 Sat fat 8.2g (41%)
4 tablespoons maple syrup
½ teaspoon cinnamon
160g oats (gluten free if needed)  🟡 Fructans 51% (27 g per serving)
½ teaspoon flaky salt
60g walnuts, roughly chopped
50g pumpkin seeds
30g sesame seeds
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
To serve:
1 or two pots of thick and creamy lactose free Greek yogurt (roughly 600g)
directions:
1. Preheat your oven to 180°C, 160°C fan, gas mark 4. Rinse the rhubarb and shake off the excess water, then trim off any brown ends and cut into 1 inch pieces.

2. Tumble the rhubarb onto a deep baking dish and sprinkle over the sugar and cardamom. Toss everything together and shuffle the rhubarb so it’s in a single layer. Cover with foil and roast for 15 minutes, then remove the foil, give everything a little shake and roast for another 5 mins or until the juices are jammy and the rhubarb is tender but still keeping its shape.

3. While the rhubarb is roasting, make the granola. Place a saucepan or shallow cast iron pan over a medium-low heat and add the coconut oil and maple syrup. When the liquid is glistening, add the cinnamon and cook for about thirty seconds, until fragrant. Add the oats and the salt, stirring to coat evenly and cook for another couple of minutes. Sprinkle in the walnuts, pumpkin seeds, sesame seeds, and vanilla. Cook for a final couple of minutes, stirring to make sure nothing catches on the bottom of the pan and stopping when everything looks toasty and golden.

4. Take the granola off the heat and spoon it into a bowl (otherwise it will continue to cook). Allow to cool slightly before serving alongside the yogurt and rhubarb.
notes: From She Can't Eat What (https://shecanteatwhat.com/low-fodmap-breakfast-cardamom-roast-rhubarb-yogurt-granola/), a low FODMAP site that follows the Monash app. For personal use.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Low FODMAP pumpkin sesame granola
ingredients:
40g coconut oil, melted and cooled  💔 Sat fat 4.1g (20%)
120ml maple syrup
2 teaspoons flaky salt
350g rolled oats (gluten free if needed)  🟠 Fructans 84% (44 g per serving)
2 teaspoons cinnamon
1 teaspoon ginger
1/2 teaspoon allspice
1/4 teaspoon ground nutmeg
100g pecans
50g sesame seeds, I like a mixture of black and white
1 large egg white, lightly whisked OR around 70g pumpkin puree  ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
directions:
1. Preheat your oven to 180C, 160C fan, gas mark 3 and line a baking tray with baking paper.

2. Combine all of the ingredients in a bowl and toss to mix until everything is evenly coated. Tip the mixture on to your baking tray and spread into a single layer.

3. Bake until everything is crispy and golden brown, around 50-60 minutes. Stir gently (keeping some clusters intact) every 20 minutes or so while baking, to make sure everything cooks evenly.

4. Let cool completely before storing in glass jars or containers of your choice. It will last about a week.

name: ℹ️ ❣ Turmeric, buckwheat, blueberry breakfast loaf
ingredients:
Dry ingredients:
25g sunflower seeds
25g walnuts
100g rolled oats, gluten free if needed  🟢 Fructans 19% (10 g per serving)
90g buckwheat flour  🟢 Fructans 18% (9 g per serving)
55g gluten free plain flour  🟢 Fructans 6% (5.5 g per serving)
1 1/2 teaspoons baking powder
1/2 teaspoons baking soda
1 teaspoon ground turmeric
1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 teaspoon ground cardamom
½ teaspoon sea salt
Wet ingredients:
160 ml almond milk
1 teaspoon lemon juice
80 ml olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 1.1g (6%)
2 ripe bananas  🟡 Fructans 69% (24 g per serving)
5 tablespoons maple syrup
3 large eggs, beaten well  ♥ Sat fat 0.5g (2%)
1 large handful blueberries, frozen or fresh
Oat topping:
50g rolled oats  🟢 Fructans 10% (5 g per serving)
3 tablespoons coconut oil  ❣ Sat fat 3.7g (18%)
2 tablespoons maple syrup
directions:
1. Preheat the oven to 200°C and grease and line a 2lb loaf tin. Add the lemon juice to the almond milk and set aside to curdle. This will make your buttermilk.

2. Add the sunflower seeds, walnuts and rolled oats to a food processor and pulse into a coarse flour. Transfer to a large mixing bowl together with the rest of the dry ingredients.

3. Add buttermilk mixture, oil, bananas and maple syrup to the food processor (no need to clean) and pulse until smooth. Make a well in your dry ingredients and pour in the wet mixture, along with the eggs. Use a spatula to carefully fold everything until combined.

4. Pour the batter into the lined loaf tin and gently push down the blueberries on top. Mix together the oat topping in a small bowl and sprinkle it on top of the blueberries.

5. Bake for about 40-45 minutes, or until golden and springy to the touch. A skewer inserted should only emerge with a few crumbs stuck to it.

6. Enjoy the loaf warm from the oven, pop a slice under the grill to toast or wait until cool, then slice and put in the freezer for later.

name: ✅ ❣ Clementine & pecan puff pastry mince pies
ingredients:
300g clementines
100g dried cranberries
70g pecans
30g coconut oil  ❣ Sat fat 2.1g (10%)
35g stem ginger, finely chopped
50g light soft brown sugar
1 teaspoon mixed spice
½ teaspoon ground ginger
½ teaspoon cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
1 tsp vanilla extract or vanilla bean paste
1/2 tsp almond extract
1-2 tablespoons whisky (optional)
400g gluten free puff pastry, defrosted (I used Genius ready made but if you wanted to make it yourself Naomi Devlin has a great recipe in her book, River Cottage Gluten Free)  ❣ Sat fat 3.7g (18%)
1 small egg  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (1%)
1 tsp brown sugar (for sprinkling)
directions:
1. To make the mincemeat: Toast the pecans in a medium sized pan over a low heat, until just turning colour (about 7-8 minutes).

2. Once golden, allow them to cool and then roughly chop. Set to one side.

3. Peel the clementines and roughly chop the flesh.

4. Add the flesh to a medium saucepan along with the coconut oil, spices, brown sugar, and finely chopped stem ginger. Stir and simmer over a medium heat with the lid on for 15 minutes.

5. Add the cranberries and simmer with the lid on for a further 10 minutes.

6. Remove the pan from the heat and stir through the almond and vanilla extract, chopped nuts and whisky.

7. Allow to cool, then decant into sterilised glass jars and store in the fridge until using.

8. To make the mince pies: preheat the oven to 200C/180 fan/gas 6. Lightly grease a 12-hole fairy-cake tin and dust with a little gluten free flour and line a flat baking tray with baking parchment.

9. Roll out your pastry on a lightly floured surface until 1/2 cm thick.

10. Cut out 12 circles using a round pastry cutter or a glass that is bigger than the holes in your fairy-cake tin. You want the pastry to come up over the sides of each one just slightly.

11. Cut out 12 slightly smaller circles and put to one side.

12. Line your fairy-cake tin with the bigger circles of pastry and place a spoonful of mincemeat into each one. Squeeze in as much as you can without the filling bubbling out!

13. Brush the edges of the pastry with a little beaten egg and press on the smaller circles of pastry, sealing round the edges.

14. Place your lined baking tray over the pies and flip the fairy cake tin upside-down. The pies should slip out of the tin, leaving you with 12 puff pies on a baking tray.

15. Press each one around the edges with a fork to make sure they’re well sealed and cut a little cross in the centre of each.

16. Brush them with more of the beaten egg and sprinkle with brown sugar.

17. Bake for 20 mins, or until golden and puffed up.

18. Allow to cool a little, then serve warm, dusted with icing sugar, and homemade whisky butter.
notes: From She Can't Eat What (https://shecanteatwhat.com/clementine-pecan-low-fodmap-mince-pies/), a low FODMAP site that follows the Monash app. For personal use.
description:
Gluten free and low FODMAP mince pies packed full of zesty clementine. Delicious with a dusting of icing sugar and slathered with whisky butter.

Place a pan over a medium heat and add the coconut oil. When the oil is glossy, add the sweet potato to the pan and fry until softened and a little charred, 3-4 minutes. Stir occasionally.; 2. Add the pineapple and cook for another 1-2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.; 3. Pour in the jar of Bay’s Kitchen Thai Massaman Stir-in Sauce, rinsing the jar out with a little water and adding that into the pan too. Cook for a couple of minutes, stirring to combine everything together.; 4. Add the prawns and fish sauce and cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until the prawns turn from translucent to opaque and pink, and are cooked through.; 5. Divide the curry between two bowls, sprinkle with the spring onion tops, peanuts and coriander and serve with a wedge of lime.; Step 6. name: ℹ️ ❣ Roasted Ratatouille Low FODMAP Vegetarian Enchiladas
ingredients:
80 g vine or Roma tomatoes  🔴 Fructose 107%
1/4 jalapeno (halved (ribs and seeds optional))
1/8 tsp ground cumin
1/8 tsp ground coriander
1 tbsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 1.9g (9%)
1 pinch sea salt (to taste)
1/4 large aubergine (cut into ½ inch cubes)
1/4 medium courgette  🟠 Fructans 77%
1/4 medium patty pan or summer squash (cut into ½ inch cubes)
1/16 red bell pepper (diced)  🟢 Fructose 23%
1/4 cup chicken or vegetable stock
1/2 tbsp fresh lime juice
1/6 cup coarsely grated cheddar cheese  ❣ Sat fat 3.5g (17%)
8 corn or almond flour tortillas (6-inch)
1/8 cup coriander leaves
directions:
1. Preheat your oven to 220°C. Line two sheet pans with parchment paper.

2. Place the tomatoes and the jalapeño on one of the sheet pans. Drizzle with olive oil and season with the cumin, coriander and ½ teaspoon salt. Arrange cut-side down and roast in the oven until slightly charred, about 40 minutes.

3. On the second sheet pan, toss the aubergine, courgette and peppers with 2 tablespoons olive oil and ½ teaspoon salt. Arrange in an even layer and roast alongside the tomatoes in the oven for about 45 minutes, until nicely caramelized. Set aside to cool.

4. Transfer the tomatoes and jalapeño to a blender or food processor and add any cooking juices from the sheet pan, along with the stock, lime juice and ½ teaspoon salt. Process until smooth. You should have about 3 cups sauce.

5. In a large mixing bowl, toss the ratatouille filling with a third of the sauce and 1/3 cup of cheese.

6. Pour another third of the tomato sauce in the bottom of a 9-by-13-inch baking dish. Spread the sauce to cover the bottom.

7. Wrap the tortillas in a dish towel and warm them in the microwave for 30 seconds until pliable. Alternatively you can warm them in the oven.

8. Divide the veggies evenly among the tortillas. Roll up the tortillas tightly around the ratatouille and line them up, seam-side down, in the baking dish. Pour the remaining tomato sauce evenly over the stuffed tortillas and sprinkle with the remaining cheese.

9. Bake the enchiladas until the cheese is melted and golden brown and the sauce is bubbling, about 20 minutes. Sprinkle with the coriander and serve immediately.

directions:
Prep the Base
1. Crack the eggs into a bowl. Add the milk or water if using, a pinch of salt, and a few grinds of pepper. Whisk until fully blended with no streaks of white.

2. Rinse and dry the spinach. Pat the cherry tomatoes dry if using.

Wilt the Spinach
3. Heat the olive oil or butter in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.

4. Add the spinach and a pinch of salt. Toss for 30 to 60 seconds, just until the leaves collapse and turn glossy. Push the wilted spinach to one side of the pan.

Soft-Scramble the Eggs
5. Turn the heat to medium-low. Pour the eggs into the empty side of the pan.

6. Let them sit for 15 seconds, then pull a silicone spatula across the bottom in slow folds. Keep folding every few seconds.

7. When the eggs are about 80 percent set but still glossy, fold in the spinach and half the feta. Remove from the heat — residual warmth finishes them.

Finish and Serve
8. Divide between two plates. Scatter the remaining feta, the fresh herbs, and the lemon zest over the top.

9. Add the halved cherry tomatoes on the side if using. Eat right away while the curds are still soft.

name: ℹ️ 💔 Gluten-free hummingbird cake
ingredients:
31 g gluten-free baking mix
1/8 tsp baking soda
1/6 tsp cinnamon
1/8 tsp salt
1/3 yellow firm bananas, mashed*  🟢 Fructans 42%
19 g canned pineapple chunks  🟢 Fructans 14%
1/4 eggs, at room temperature  ♥ Sat fat 0.4g (2%)
13 ml sunflower oil  ♥ Sat fat 1.3g (6%)
17 g light brown caster sugar
8.3 g white sugar
1/6 tsp vanilla extract
10 g pecan nuts + extra for garnish
38 g lactose-free cream cheese  💔 Sat fat 7.6g (38%)
12 g unsalted butter, at room temperature  💔 Sat fat 6.1g (31%)
17 g powdered sugar
1/4 tsp low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)
1 pinch salt (to taste)
1/4 cake tins – 8 inches or 20 cm in size
directions:
For the cake
1. Preheat the oven to 180°C.

2. Grease three 8 inches or 20-cm cake tins.

3. Cut out circles the size of the baking tins from a sheet of baking paper and place them in the baking tins.

4. Grease the baking paper a little and grease the edges of the baking tin. This way you can be sure that the cakes come out of the tin properly.

5. Put the baking mix, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt together in a bowl and stir together.

6. Mash the bananas. Save 2 tbsp of the pineapple juice from the can. Drain the pieces of pineapple. Place the mashed bananas, pineapple juice, and pineapple chunks in another bowl.

7. Also add the eggs, sunflower oil, 2 types of sugar, and vanilla extract and stir together.

8. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir until you have a batter.

9. Coarsely chop the pecans and stir them into the batter.

10. Divide the batter among the three cake tins. You can also bake them one at a time if you only have 1 cake tin of the right size at home.

11. Bake the cakes in the oven for 25-30 minutes. The cake is ready when a skewer comes out clean.

12. Let cool completely.

13. Remove the cakes from the tins after cooling and cut off a small layer from the top so your cakes are flat.

14. Mix the cream cheese with the butter until soft.

15. Add powdered sugar, milk, vanilla extract, and salt. Mix this together gently.

16. Then continue mixing on a high setting for a few more minutes until you have a creamy frosting.

17. Place a layer of cake on the cake stand or serving plate on which you want to serve the cake. Cover the top of the cake with a layer of frosting.

18. Place the next cake layer on top. Cover this with frosting as well and finish with the third cake layer.

19. Spread frosting on the top and sides of the cake. Use a palette knife for this and smooth the sides and top of the cake nicely.

20. Garnish the cake with chopped pecans.

name: ✅ 💔 Gluten-free drip cake
ingredients:
28 g soft butter  💔 Sat fat 14.3g (71%)
28 g granulated sugar (for the cake)
1/2 eggs, at room temperature  ♥ Sat fat 0.8g (4%)
1/2 tbsp low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (0%)
1/8 tsp vanilla extract
34 g gluten-free self-raising flour  🟢 Fructans 34%
1 pinch salt (to taste)
3x 6-inch cake tins (I only have two, so I baked the first two layers first and the last one separately)
10 ml egg whites (I used 4 egg whites from medium-sized eggs)  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
17 g granulated sugar (for the meringue buttercream)
28 g soft buttter
5/8 tsp blueberry jam (make sure no high FODMAP ingredients are added) + extra to put in between the cake layers  🟢 Fructose 2%
A candy thermometer
12 g dark chocolate  ❣ Sat fat 2.2g (11%)
12 ml lactose-free whipping cream  ❣ Sat fat 2.9g (14%)
1 cube butter
Strawberries
Raspberries
White roses
Gluten-free & low FODMAP double cookies (Oreo’s)
1 tsp heart sprinkles or other decoration of your choice (of your choice)
3x 6-inch (15 cm) cake tins (I only have two, so I baked the first two layers first and the last one separately)
directions:
For the cake
1. Pre-heat the oven to 175°C. Grease the cake tins and line them with baking parchment.

2. Mix the butter and the sugar creamy. Then add the eggs one by one while you mix in between. Add the lactose-free milk and the vanilla extract and mix again.

3. Put the self-raising flour and the salt together in a bowl and add this to the batter little by little, while you keep mixing. Mix until you have a smooth batter.

4. Divide the batter over the three cake tins. It is important that your layers have the same height, so use an equal amount of batter for each layer. I used 450 gram of batter in each cake tin.

5. Smoothen the batter in the cake tins with a spatula. Bake the cakes for about 30-35 minutes until a toothpick comes uit clean. Depending on how many cakes you bake in the oven at a time, it might take longer or shorter until the cakes are done.

6. Remove the cakes from the oven and leave to cool down in the tin. When almost cold, you can remove them from the tins and leave them to cool down completely. Make sure that the cakes are not warm anymore when you start decorating.

The buttercream
7. While the cakes are cooling down we can make the buttercream. Split the eggs and make sure that you don’t get any egg yolk in the egg whites. You need 120 ml of egg whites.

8. Mix the egg whites together with the sugar in a glass bowl. If you have a standmixer, use the bowl of your standmixer (if it is heat-proof). Just mix the egg whites and the sugar together shortly You are going to heat the egg whites and you don’t want them to start cooking.

9. Fill a pan with a layer of water and bring it to a simmer. Place the glass bowl on top of the pan. The water should be kept at a simmer and should not touch the bottom of the glass bowl.

10. While stirring regularly, heat the egg white mixture until it reaches a temperature of 68-70°C (155-70°C). I use a candy thermometer to measure the temperature. The mixture should be very warm and the sugar should have dissolved.

11. Carefully remove the bowl from the pan. Put it under your standmixer or if you don’t have a standmixer, grab your handmixer. Beat the mixture on high speed for about 8 minutes. When it is done the meringue should be shiny and stand in medium-stiff peaks. The bowl should have cooled down to room temperature.

12. Set the mixture to low and begin adding in the butter, a few small chunks at a time. Make sure the butter is at room temperature.

13. Once all the butter has been mixed in, add the vanilla extract and 2 tbsp of blueberry jam.

14. Turn up the mixer to medium speed and mix until your buttercream is silky smooth. This might take a few minutes.

Building the cake
15. Make sure that the three layers of cake are all flat. Trim off the top with a serrated knife, so all layers are flat and equal. Put one layer of cake onto your turntable. Divide a tablespoon of blueberry jam on top. Leave the edges free.

16. Then divide a layer of buttercream over the cake layer. Start and the edges and work towards the middle.

17. Put the second cake layer on top of the frosting and divide a tablespoon of jam over it. Repeat with a layer of buttercream. Then put the final layer of cake on top.

18. Now we are going to do the crumb coating. Carefully spread a thin layer of buttercream on the top of the cake and around the sides. Put the cake into the fridge for at least 15 minutes, so the crumb coating can set.

19. Depending on how dark you want your frosting on the outside of the cake to be, you can add another tablespoon of blueberry jam to the buttercream.

20. Cover the top and the side of your cake with buttercream using your spatula. When the cake is covered in buttercream you can use your scraper to smooth your frosting. Place your scraper against the side of the cake in a 45 degree angle. Don’t apply too much pressure and turn your turntable around. Clean the excess icing off your scraper regularly. When the sides of the cake are smooth, you can use your spatula to carefully remove excess frosting on the top of the cake.

21. Put the cake in the fridge again to cool, at least for half an hour. To make sure that you can make your chocolate drip succesfully, it is important that the cake is cold.

The chocolate drip & decoration
22. Put the cubes of chocolate into a heatproof bowl. Take a small pan and heat the whipping cream on the stove. Heat the cream until it almost starts bubbling (it shouldn’t cook).

23. Pour the whipping cream on top of the chocolate and stir together until the chocolate has melted. Add a small cube of butter and stir until this has melted too.

24. Take the cake out of the fridge.

25. Take a tablespoon and carefully make drips on the side of the cake. I found this tutorial very helpful. After you have made the drips, spread a thin layer of chocolate over the top of the cake.

26. Now decorate the cake with Oreo’s, the fruit and the flours. Do this when the chocolate is still wet because then it will stay in place after the chocolate has hardened.

ingredients:

ingredients:

name: ✅ ♡ Breakfast - Gluten-Free Bagels
ingredients:
420 g gluten-free 1:1 flour blend, rice, potato, and tapioca based, with xanthan gum already included
20 g whole psyllium husk (not powder; see the tips if you only have powder)
2 1/4 tsp instant yeast
1 tbsp cane sugar, plus 1 tsp for the yeast
1 1/2 tsp fine salt
1 tbsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
360 ml warm water, about 105F (40C)
8 cups water
1 tbsp cane sugar or pure maple syrup
1 tbsp white sesame seeds
1 tbsp black sesame seeds
2 tsp poppy seeds
1 tsp flaky sea salt
1 tsp dried spring onion, green tops only, for onion aroma (optional)  🟢 Fructose 0% (0.1 g per serving)
low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed) or water, for brushing
directions:
Make the dough
1. In a large bowl, combine the warm water, 1 tsp cane sugar, and the yeast. Let it sit until foamy, about 5 minutes.

2. Whisk the psyllium husk into the yeast water and rest 1 to 2 minutes, until it thickens into a soft gel.

3. In a separate bowl, whisk the flour blend, the remaining 1 tbsp sugar, and the salt. Pour in the psyllium mixture and the oil, then mix to a shaggy dough.

4. Knead in the bowl for 2 to 3 minutes until smooth. The dough stays tacky, which is normal for gluten-free dough; resist adding much extra flour.

Shape and rise
5. Divide the dough into 8 equal pieces (about 100g each). Roll each into a ball, then push a floured finger through the center and widen the hole to about 1.5 to 2 inches.

6. Set the bagels on a parchment-lined tray, cover loosely, and rise in a warm spot for 45 to 60 minutes, until slightly puffed.

7. While they rise, heat the oven to 220°C and bring the boiling bath to a gentle simmer with the sugar or maple syrup stirred in.

Boil, top, and bake
8. Boil the bagels in batches for 30 to 60 seconds per side. Gluten-free dough is delicate, so keep the boil brief and lift them out with a slotted spoon to drain.

9. Brush the tops with almond milk or water (or beaten egg), then sprinkle on the everything topping.

10. Bake for 22 to 26 minutes, until deep golden and firm. Cool on a rack at least 20 minutes before slicing, since the crumb sets as it cools.

name: ✅ 💔 Dutch Rice Pudding Pie (low FODMAP, gluten-free, lactose-free)
ingredients:
210 g gluten-free flour  🟢 Fructans 21% (21 g per serving)
¾ tsp xanthan gum
¼ tsp baking powder
¼ tsp salt
30 g powdered sugar
85 g butter, cold and in cubes  💔 Sat fat 4.3g (22%)
120 ml water with ice cubes in it
700 ml low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.7g (4%)
115 g dessert rice
100 g sugar + 30 gr extra sugar
1 vanilla pod
2 eggs, the yolk and egg white separated  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
400 ml lactose-free whipped cream  💔 Sat fat 9.6g (48%)
3 tbsp sugar
directions:
1. Put flour, xanthan gum, baking powder, salt and powdered sugar in a bowl to make the crust and stir everything together. Add the cubes of butter. Knead this into the flour mixture with your hands, pressing the cubes of butter between your fingers and mixing them into the dough.

2. Add the ice water (take the ice cubes out, this is only to make the water cold enough) and knead the dough until it starts to come together. If the dough remains too dry you can add extra water by the tablespoon.

3. Put the dough on a piece of plastic foil, flatten it and wrap it in the plastic. Put the dough in the freezer for 30 minutes until it’s firmer. At this point, you can keep the dough in the fridge for several days if you don’t want to use it immediately or you can keep it in the freezer for a longer period. Defreeze it in the fridge overnight before using it.

4. In the meantime, you can start making the rice filling. Put the milk in a pan and bring to boil. Scrape the vanilla out of the vanilla pod and add this to the milk. Add the dessert rice and sugar (100 gr) when the milk starts to boil. Lower the heat (make sure the milk continues to boil) and leave the rice to boil until most of the milk has evaporated. Stir now and then. The consistency should be like a porridge, not entirely dry. Turn off the heat and leave the rice filling to cool down.

5. Grease the pie tin with butter. Make sure you also grease the sides well. Pre-heat the oven to 190°C.

6. Put the dough on a piece of baking parchment and cover it with plastic foil. Use a rolling pin to roll the dough into a circle that is slightly bigger than the baking tin (about 10-11 inch diameter).

7. Remove the plastic foil. Roll your dough around the rolling pin carefully and put the dough on top of the pie tin. Press the dough into the tin carefully. There will always be some excess dough on the sides. Roll over the sides with a rolling pin carefully to remove the excess dough.

8. Prick the bottom of the crust with a fork.

9. Whisk the egg yolks creamy with 30 gr of sugar and stir this through the lukewarm rice filling.

10. Beat the egg whites until stiff and spoon half of the egg whites through the rice filling. Divide half of the rice filling over the pie crust.

11. Spoon the other half of the egg whites into the remaining half of the rice filling and divide this over the crust too.

12. Put the rice pudding pie in the oven for about 25-30 minutes. Keep an eye on the pie during the last minutes of baking. The rice pudding pie is done when the filling has browned and the dough is loosened from the sides of the tin.

13. Take the pie out of the oven and remove the side of the tin immediately. You can do this easily by putting the tin on top of a turned bowl. Turn the pie onto a wire rack to cool down.

14. When the rice pudding pie has cooled down entirely you can put the topping on. Whip the cream with two tablespoons of sugar and divide this on top of the pie.

15. Grate some chocolate and sprinkle this on top of the cream.

name: ✅ ♡ Sweet - No-Bake Cookies
ingredients:
1/2 cup unsalted butter  ❣ Sat fat 3.1g (15%)
300 g granulated cane or white sugar
1/4 cup pure maple syrup (not honey or agave)
1/2 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (0%)
1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
1/4 tsp salt
1/2 cup natural smooth peanut butter (just peanuts, plus salt)  ♥ Sat fat 0.4g (2%)
1 tsp vanilla extract
2 1/2 cups certified gluten-free rolled oats  🟢 Fructans 22% (11 g per serving)
Portion note: this batch makes about 20 cookies, and a serving is 1 to 2 cookies. Oats are low-FODMAP up to 1 (52
directions:
Cook the base
1. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper and set them near the stove so you can portion quickly once the mixture is ready.

2. In a medium saucepan, combine the butter, sugar, maple syrup, lactose-free milk, cocoa, and salt. Stir over medium heat until the butter melts and the sugar dissolves.

3. Bring to a rolling boil and let it boil, stirring, for 60 to 90 seconds. Boiling is what sets the cookies as they cool. Underboiling leaves them sticky, and overboiling makes them dry and crumbly.

4. Remove the pan from the heat.

Add peanut butter and oats
5. Stir in the peanut butter and vanilla until the mixture is smooth and glossy.

6. Add the oats and fold until every oat is coated.

7. Work quickly, since the mixture firms up as it cools.

Portion and set
8. Drop rounded tablespoons onto the parchment, spacing them slightly apart, for about 20 mounds.

9. Let the cookies set at room temperature for about 30 minutes, or 15 minutes in the fridge, until firm to the touch.

directions:

2. Clean the green beans by cutting off the ends. Cut into small pieces.

3. Bring a pan of water to the boil and add the green beans with a pinch of salt. Boil for 6 minutes and drain. Set aside.

4. Heat 1/2 tbsp butter in a wok or large frying pan.

5. Beat the eggs in a bowl with the lactose-free milk and beat well.

6. Add the eggs to the pan and keep stirring continuously until you have scrambled eggs.

7. Place the scrambled eggs in a bowl and set aside.

8. Add another tablespoon of butter to the pan and heat the pan until the butter has melted.

9. Add the green beans and carrots and cook for about 5 minutes until the vegetables are tender.

10. Add the final tablespoon of butter to the pan and wait until it has melted.

11. Add the rice, soy sauce and spring onion to the rice and mix very well.

12. Increase the heat slightly and cook the rice for about 4 minutes, stirring frequently.

13. Finally add the scrambled eggs and stir everything together.

14. Serve right away.

name: ✅ ♡ Low FODMAP vegan brownies with salted caramel sauce
ingredients:
6.7 g gluten-free flour  🟢 Fructans 7%
12 g sugar
10 ml low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (0%)

13 g dark chocolate  ❣ Sat fat 2.3g (12%)
1/2 tsp cacao powder
1/12 tsp vanilla extract (for the brownie)
1/8 pinch of salt
1/8 can full-fat coconut milk
12 g maple syrup
1/4 tsp coconut oil  ♥ Sat fat 1g (5%)
1/6 tsp vanilla extract (for the salted caramel sauce)
1 pinch coarse sea salt (to taste)
directions:
1. Pre-heat the oven to 180°C. Line a square or rectangular brownie tin with baking parchment.

2. Mix the sugar, oil, almond milk and vanilla extract together in a bowl.

3. Melt the chocolate au bain-marie or in a pan on a very low heat.

4. Add the chocolate, gluten-free flour, cacao powder and salt to the sugar mixture and stir until you have a smooth batter.

5. Poor the batter into the tin. Bake the brownies fora bout 25 minutes. I, personally, love sticky brownies and then these brownies are perfect after 25 minutes of baking. If you prefer them slightly more dry, you can try baking them for 5 more minutes.

6. Remove the brownies from the oven and leave them to cool.

7. In the meantime, you can make the caramel sauce.

8. Mix the coconut milk with the maple syrup and a pinch of salt.

9. Put this into a pan and bring to boil. Lower the heat and leave the caramel sauce to simmer for 40 minutes, while stirring now and then.

10. Add the coconut oil after 40 minutes and leave to simmer for another 5 minutes, until the caramel gets a beautiful caramel colour. Stir regularly.

11. Remove the caramel sauce from the heat, add the vanilla extract and stir in the coarse sea salt. Add salt little by little and taste in between to see if the salted caramel sauce is salty enough.

12. Pour the caramel sauce into a bowl and leave to cool for 5 minutes. Stir well after five minutes until you have a glossy sauce.

13. Pour the caramel sauce on top of the brownies.

14. You can store the brownies in the fridge before serving. If you have any left-over caramel sauce, it is best to reheat it in a pan for a few minutes before using it again.

directions:
1. Preheat oven to 175°C℉ (180℃). Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.

6. Bake cookies until tops are firm and dry to touch (cookies will firm more as they cool), 9-10 minutes. Transfer parchment with cookies onto wire racks to cool completely.

7. When cookies are cooled, stir chocolate chips in a medium heatproof bowl set over a saucepan of simmering water (water should not touch bowl) until melted and smooth (or heat in a microwave in 10-second increments and stir until smooth). Stir in peppermint flavouring. Let cool for a few minutes before handling.

8. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper (you can use the same sheet you baked on). Dip tops of cookies into chocolate glaze and place on prepared sheet. Chill cookies in freezer to firm them up, at least 15 minutes.

9. Once firm, store cookies in the fridge.

name: ✅ ❣ Breakfast - Crepes
ingredients:

1 tbsp cane or white sugar
1/4 tsp salt
1 tsp vanilla extract
1/4 tsp xanthan gum, only if your flour blend does not already contain a gum  🟢 Fructans 0% (0.2 g per serving)
10 medium fresh strawberries, sliced (about)
1 blueberries (up to; about 20 berries)
1 small handful raspberries

directions:
Make the batter
1. Whisk the eggs, lactose-free milk, melted butter, sugar, salt, and vanilla in a bowl until smooth.

2. Add the flour blend (and xanthan gum if using) and whisk until no lumps remain. The batter should be thin, close to heavy cream. Whisk in a splash more milk if it seems thick.

3. Let the batter rest for 20 to 30 minutes at room temperature. This hydrates the gluten-free flour and gives a smoother crepe.

Cook the crepes
4. Heat a nonstick or well-seasoned skillet over medium heat and brush lightly with butter.

5. Pour in about 1/4 cup of batter and immediately tilt and swirl the pan so the batter spreads into a thin, even circle.

6. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the edges lift and the underside is golden. Loosen with a spatula, flip, and cook the second side for about 30 seconds.

7. Slide onto a plate and repeat, brushing the pan with butter between crepes. Whisk the batter again if it thickens as it sits.

Fill and serve
8. Lay a crepe flat and add a line of berries down the center, keeping to the portions listed above.

9. Drizzle with maple syrup, add lactose-free yogurt or cream if you like, then fold or roll. Serve warm.

directions:
Mix the Batter
1. Whisk the flour blend, sugar, baking powder, cinnamon, and salt together in a large bowl.

Cook

7. Transfer directly to a wire rack set in a 95°C oven to stay crisp while you cook the rest. Don't stack them on a plate — the trapped steam makes the crust soggy.

8. Repeat with the remaining batter, re-buttering the plates every second or third waffle. The recipe makes about 8 standard waffles or 4 large Belgian waffles depending on your iron (2 servings per large Belgian, 2 standard per serving).

name: ✅ ❣ Mocktail - Virgin Eggnog (Lactose-Free)
ingredients:
4 large pasteurized eggs, separated  ♥ Sat fat 1.6g (8%)
1/4 cup pure maple syrup, divided
2 cups low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 1.2g (6%)
4 tbsp lactose-free heavy cream (or regular heavy cream)  💔 Sat fat 5g (25%)
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg, plus more for garnish
1/4 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1 pinch fine sea salt (to taste)
1 portion ice (for serving)
directions:
Warm the Dairy
1. In a medium saucepan, combine the lactose-free milk, cream, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt.

2. Set over medium-low heat and warm until steaming and just barely bubbling at the edges, about 5 to 7 minutes. Do not let it boil.

3. Remove from the heat and set aside.

Temper the Yolks
4. In a medium bowl, whisk the egg yolks with 3 tablespoons of the maple syrup until pale and thickened, about 1 minute.

5. Slowly pour about 1 cup of the warm milk mixture into the yolks in a thin stream, whisking constantly. This tempers the eggs so they don't scramble.

6. Pour the tempered yolk mixture back into the saucepan with the remaining warm milk.

Cook Gently
7. Return the saucepan to low heat. Cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon or silicone spatula, until the mixture thickens enough to coat the back of the spoon and reaches 70°C on an instant-read thermometer, about 3 to 5 minutes.

8. Immediately remove from the heat and stir in the vanilla extract. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a large bowl or pitcher to catch any cooked egg bits.

Cool, Then Whip and Fold (Optional)
9. Let the custard cool to room temperature, or at least below 30°C, so the whites don't deflate on contact.

10. In a clean bowl, whisk the egg whites with the remaining maple syrup until soft peaks form, about 2 to 3 minutes by hand or 1 minute with an electric mixer.

11. Gently fold the whipped whites into the cooled custard base until just combined. The eggnog will look frothy and light. (Skip this step entirely for a fully cooked, thinner version — see Tips.)

Chill and Serve
12. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until fully chilled.

13. Stir well before serving. Pour into small glasses or mugs, over ice if desired, and dust the top with extra nutmeg.

directions:

ingredients:
10 large eggs  ❣ Sat fat 2.7g (13%)
150 g baby spinach
120 g crumbled feta  ❣ Sat fat 2.8g (14%)
150 g red bell pepper (about 2 medium), small-dice  🟡 Fructose 58% (25 g per serving)
174 g cherry tomatoes (about 30), halved  🟡 Fructose 64% (29 g per serving)
4 spring onions, green tops only, thinly sliced  🟢 Fructose 11% (8 g per serving)

directions:
Prep the Pan and Oven
1. Heat the oven to 190°C. Brush a standard 12-cup muffin tin generously with 1 tablespoon of the olive oil, getting into the corners of each well. Parchment liners work too, but silicone or a well-greased metal pan releases best.

2. Rinse and dry the spinach, bell pepper, cherry tomatoes, and spring onion greens.

Wilt the Spinach and Peppers
3. Heat the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat.

4. Add the bell pepper and a pinch of salt. Toss for 3 to 4 minutes until it softens slightly.

5. Add the spinach in handfuls, tossing until each batch collapses. Cook for another 1 to 2 minutes until the pan is mostly dry. Transfer to a plate, press out any excess liquid with the back of a spoon, and let it cool for 5 minutes.

Whisk the Eggs
6. Crack the eggs into a large bowl. Add the milk or water, kosher salt, and several grinds of pepper. Whisk until fully blended with no streaks of white.

7. Stir in the cooled spinach and peppers, two-thirds of the feta, and the spring onion greens. Fold in the chopped bacon if using.

Fill and Bake
8. Divide the mixture evenly among the 12 muffin wells — each should be about three-quarters full. A 1/3-cup measure gets you close in a single scoop.

9. Top each cup with a few halved cherry tomatoes (cut-side up) and the remaining feta.

10. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the tops are set and lightly golden and a muffin springs back when pressed. A toothpick should come out clean.

11. Let the muffins rest in the pan for 5 minutes so they firm up, then run a thin knife or offset spatula around each well and lift them out. Scatter the fresh herbs over the top.

name: ✅ 💔 Soup - Clam Chowder

3 slices plain bacon (no added garlic or onion powder), chopped  💔 Sat fat 9.9g (50%)
2 spring onion green tops, leeks, or 4 spring onion green tops, thinly sliced (use the GREEN tops only)
2 medium celery stalks, finely diced  🟢 Mannitol 39% (20 g per serving)
3 medium waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch cubes

1/2 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves
2 tablespoons olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.9g (5%)

1/2 cup lactose-free cream (or more lactose-free milk)  ❣ Sat fat 3.6g (18%)

directions:
**Prep (bowls):**

**Medium bowl — bacon:**
- Chop the bacon.

**Large bowl — aromatics (fry / soften):**
- Thinly slice the leek or spring onion greens. Finely dice the celery.

**Large bowl — potatoes:**
- Peel and cube the potatoes.

**Medium bowl — clams:**
- Drain the clams; reserve the juice.

**Small bowl — thickener & herbs:**
- Have the gluten-free flour ready. Set out the bay leaf and thyme.

**By the hob (no bowl):** olive oil, bottled clam juice, reserved clam juice, low-FODMAP broth or water, lactose-free milk, lactose-free cream, salt, pepper.

**Medium bowl — finish:**
- Chop the parsley.

**1. Crisp bacon:** Cook the bacon in a heavy pot over medium heat until crisp, 5–7 minutes. Transfer to a plate; leave about a tablespoon of fat in the pot.

**2. Soften veg:** Add olive oil and the aromatics bowl; soften about 4 minutes without much colour.

**3. Build base:** Sprinkle over the flour; stir 1 minute. Slowly whisk in bottled clam juice, reserved clam juice and broth. Add the potatoes, bay leaf and thyme. Simmer uncovered until potatoes are tender, 15–18 minutes, stirring so nothing sticks.

**4. Finish:** On low, stir in milk and cream; heat 3–4 minutes without boiling. Add the clams; warm 2–3 minutes only. Discard the bay leaf. Season. Serve topped with reserved bacon and parsley from the finish bowl.

name: ✅ ❣ Sweet - Vanilla Cupcakes
ingredients:
245 g gluten-free 1:1 flour blend, one without added inulin or chicory root  🟢 Fructans 20% (20 g per serving)
1/2 tsp xanthan gum (skip if your blend already lists it)
1 1/2 tsp gluten-free baking powder
1/4 tsp salt
1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened  💔 Sat fat 5.1g (26%)
3/4 cup white or superfine (caster) sugar
2 large eggs, at room temperature  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (1%)
2 tsp vanilla extract
3/4 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed), at room temperature (for the cupcakes)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (1%)
2 cups confectioners' (powdered) sugar, sifted
1 to 2 tbsp lactose-free milk (for the vanilla buttercream)
1 pinch salt (to taste)
directions:
Make the batter
1. Heat the oven to 175°C and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.

2. Whisk the flour blend, xanthan gum (if using), baking powder, and salt in a bowl and set aside.

3. Beat the softened butter and sugar with a mixer on medium until pale and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each, then beat in the vanilla.

4. On low speed, add the flour mixture in three additions alternating with the lactose-free milk, starting and ending with the flour. Mix just until the batter is smooth and no dry streaks remain.

Bake
5. Divide the batter evenly among the 12 liners, filling each about two-thirds full.

6. Bake for 18 to 22 minutes, until the tops spring back when lightly pressed and a toothpick comes out clean.

7. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then move the cupcakes to a wire rack and cool completely before frosting.

Make the buttercream and frost
8. Beat the softened butter on medium until smooth, about 1 minute. Add the sifted confectioners' sugar in two additions on low speed, then beat in the vanilla and salt.

9. Add lactose-free milk 1 teaspoon at a time and beat on medium-high for 2 minutes, until light and spreadable.

10. Pipe or spread the buttercream onto the fully cooled cupcakes.

13. Divide the rice over two plates.

directions:
Mix the Batter
1. Mash the banana in a medium bowl with a fork until mostly smooth; a few small lumps are fine.

Cook

ingredients:

directions:
1. Whisk the egg yolks together in a bowl. Add the milk, sugar, flour and salt and stir together.

2. Whisk the egg whites in a clean bowl until they form soft peaks. Make sure to clean your bowl and mixer well before whisking the egg whites. If the bowl or mixer is still greasy, the egg whites won’t get stiff.

3. Fold the egg whites into the flour mixture.

4. Heat some butter or margarine in a large frying pan. If you have a small frying pan it is better to bake the kaiserschmarrn in two loads because if the pan is too full it will be difficult. Pour the batter into the pan. Leave it to bake for a minute on medium heat and flip the pancake over with a spatula. Don’t worry if this doesn’t go well, you will tear the pancake apart later on anyway.

5. Bake the other side of the pancake for another minute. Take two forks and tear the pancake into pieces carefully. Fry the pieces for about two minutes until they brown.

6. In the meantime, make the sauce by heating the raspberries in another pan. Carefully mash them with a fork when they get warm. Add a tablespoon of cornstarch to thicken the sauce and some powdered sugar to sweeten it a bit.

7. Serve the kaiserschmarrn immediately with the raspberry sauce and some powdered sugar.

name: ✅ 💔 Low FODMAP Mashed Potatoes
ingredients:
151 g Yukon Gold potatoes (about 6-7 medium potatoes)
1/8 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed) (plus more as needed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
2/3 tbsp unsalted butter  💔 Sat fat 5.1g (25%)
1 pinch salt (to taste)
1 tbsp extra butter, snipped chives, freshly-cracked black pepper, plain ground horseradish (for serving)  💔 Sat fat 4.8g (24%)
directions:
1. Scrub potatoes well under warm running water. Optional: Peel the potatoes for a smoother mashed potato. I like to keep the potato skins on for an added boost of fiber. Cut potatoes into 1 ½ to 2-inch pieces.

2. Fill a Dutch oven (or large pot) with water and bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, add the potatoes and cook for 10-15 minutes, or until the potatoes are fork-tender. Carefully drain the potatoes and transfer them to the bowl of a stand mixer (or return to the Dutch oven for mashing by hand).

3. If "mashing" with a stand-mixer: Affix the paddle attachment. Add the milk and butter to the potatoes. Start to “mash” the potatoes on low, gradually increasing speed, as needed. I use a KitchenAid 10-speed mixer and prefer to use the 2nd-speed setting (low). Continue to mix until the potatoes are almost mashed but still a little lumpy, about 30 seconds to 1 minute. Turn off the mixer. Scrape down the sides of the bowl with a spatula. Adjust flavor with salt. If the potatoes seem dry, add additional milk (1-2 tablespoons at a time) to achieve your desired creaminess. Either finish mixing by hand (for a more rustic texture), or return to mixing with the stand mixer on low (for a smoother mashed potato). If finishing with the stand mixer, keep an eye on the potatoes as they can quickly become glossy and gluey - indications the potatoes are over-mashed.

4. If mashing by hand: Add the milk and butter to the drained potatoes in the Dutch oven. Use a potato masher to mash until everything is combined and the potatoes reach your desired level of smoothness. Adjust flavor with salt. If the potatoes seem dry, add additional milk (1-2 tablespoons at a time) to achieve your desired creaminess.

5. Serve warm with optional snipped chives, extra butter, freshly-cracked black pepper, or (my family's favorite) ground horseradish. Storage: Refrigerate in an airtight container for use within 3 days.

name: ✅ ❣ Gluten-free Dutch tompouce
ingredients:
6 square sheets of gluten-free puff pastry (make sure the ingredients are low FODMAP)
Two disposable piping bags
350 ml low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.6g (3%)
1 vanilla pod
55 g sugar, divided into 35 g and 20 g (for the creme patissiere)
35 g custard powder
200 g lactose-free whipping cream (refrigerate well before using)  💔 Sat fat 8g (40%)
3.5 gelatin sheets
30 g sugar (for the whipping cream)
100 g powdered sugar
1 tbsp carrot juice*
directions:
The puff pastry
1. Pre-heat the oven to 210°C and make sure the puff pastry is thawed.

2. Cut the square pieces of puff pastry in half, so you get 12 slices.

3. Prick into the pieces of puff pastry with a fork. By doing this, you make sure the puff pastry won’t puff up too much.

4. Bake the puff pastry 12-15 minutes until they have browned nicely. Your puff pastry might have slightly different baking instructions, then follow the instructions on the package.

The creme patissiere
5. Put the milk together with 35 g sugar and the vanilla from the vanilla pod in a pan. Stir everything together and bring the milk to boil.

6. Put the custard powder in a bowl and add a splash of milk. Whisk this together very well and make sure there are no lumps in the mixture.

7. Add a bit of the hot milk to the custard mixture and whisk together well.

8. Add the custard mixture to the milk in the pan and continue to stir well with a whisk.

9. Bring the mixture to boil again and let it simmer until it gets a bit thicker.

10. Pour the cream onto a baking sheet and cover with plastic foil. Leave to cool.

11. Put the gelatin in a bowl with cold water and put aside for 10 minutes.

12. Squeeze gelatin sheets and put them in a pan. Melt the gelatin sheets on low heat.

13. Add 200 g of the whipping cream together with 20 g sugar to a bowl and whisk until the cream forms stiff peaks.

14. Put the creme into a bowl, stir through and stir in the melted gelatin.

15. Stir in the whipped cream too.

16. Put the creme patissiere mixture on a baking sheet and leave to cool in the fridge for 5 minutes.

The Whipping cream
17. Mix the other 200 g of whipping cream together with 30 g of sugar until the cream forms soft peaks.

Building the tompouce
18. Put the creme patissiere in one piping bag and the whipping cream in the other.

19. Pipe the creme patissiere on the bottom layers of puff pastry in straight lines. Pipe the whipped cream on top of the creme patissiere.

20. Put a layer of puff pastry on top of each tompouce.

21. Use a palette knife to remove surplus cream from the sides of the tompouces.

The icing
22. Mix the carrot juice with the powdered sugar, until you get the desired thickness of the icing. Spread the icing on top of the upper layers of puff pastry.

23. Put the tompouces in the fridge to get firm.

directions:
Mix the dry ingredients and cut in the butter

2. Whisk the flour blend, xanthan gum, baking powder, the 1/4 cup sugar, and salt in a large bowl.

3. Add the cold cubed butter. Rub it into the flour with your fingertips (or cut it in with two knives) until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs with a few pea-sized pieces left.

Add the wet ingredients and fold in the berries
4. In a separate bowl, whisk the egg, lactose-free milk, and vanilla until combined.

Shape and bake

8. Space the wedges on the baking sheet. Brush the tops with the extra tablespoon of milk and sprinkle with the remaining sugar.

9. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until the tops are golden and a wedge feels set in the center. Cool on the sheet for 5 minutes before serving.

25 g gluten-free flour (I use Schär Mix It Universal)  🟢 Fructans 25%

1/5 tsp baking powder
1/6 tsp xanthan gom
1/8 tsp salt
13 g butter, cold  💔 Sat fat 6.6g (33%)
8 ml low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (0%)

directions:
1. Preheat the oven to 200°C.

2. Combine flour, sugar, baking powder, xanthan gum and salt in a bowl. Stir together with a spoon.

3. Cut the butter into very small cubes. Knead this with your hands through the dough until you get a crumbly mixture.

4. Then add the milk and knead until you have a dough ball.

5. Flour the counter with some gluten-free flour.

6. Roll out the dough to a slice of approx. 15 by 30 cm (5.9 by 11.8 inch).

Fold the dough in half so that you have a square of about 15 by 15 cm (5.9 by 5.9 inch). Roll out a little so that the two slices are stuck together well. You should now have a slice of dough about 2 cm (0.8 inch) thick.
7. Use a cutter to make 10 scones from the dough. I first took out about 7 and then rolled out the leftover dough again into a 2 cm slice and removed the last 3 scones.

8. Do you feel the dough getting too soft or too warm? Then put it in the fridge for 15 minutes in between. It is important that the dough is not too warm.

9. Mix 1 egg with 1 tbsp water in a bowl.

10. Brush the scones with the egg mixture.

11. Bake the scones in the oven for 18 minutes.

12. Remove from oven and let cool.

13. Whip the cream with the sugar.

14. Cut the scones in half and serve with whipped cream and lemon curd or jam.

Griddle in rings

ingredients:

1 cup confectioners' (powdered) sugar (for the vanilla glaze)

1/4 tsp vanilla extract (for the chocolate glaze)
directions:
Mix the batter
1. Heat the oven to 175°C. Grease a 6-cavity standard donut pan well, including the center posts.

2. In a bowl, whisk together the flour blend, xanthan gum (if using), baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon.

3. In a second bowl, whisk the sugar, egg, lactose-free milk, melted butter, and vanilla until smooth.

4. Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir just until no dry streaks remain. The batter will be thick and scoopable.

Fill and bake
5. Spoon the batter into a piping bag or a zip-top bag with a corner snipped off, then pipe it into each cavity until about two-thirds full so the center hole stays open.

6. Bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the tops spring back when lightly pressed and a toothpick comes out clean.

7. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then turn the donuts out onto a rack and cool completely before glazing.

Glaze
8. Whisk the confectioners' sugar with the vanilla and (for chocolate) the cocoa powder.

9. Add the lactose-free milk a teaspoon at a time until the glaze is smooth and thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.

10. Dip the top of each cooled donut into the glaze, let the excess drip off, then set back on the rack for 10 to 15 minutes to firm up.

directions:
1. Bring a large pot of water to a boil.

2. Peel the potatoes and cut them into quarters. Make sure you have approximately the same size quarters.

3. Add these to the pan and add the kale to the pan as well. Let it cook for 20 minutes.

4. Meanwhile, clean the oyster mushrooms and cut into pieces.

5. Heat a pan and add the bacon to it. Fry for five minutes and then add the mushrooms. Bake for 5 minutes until golden brown. Turn off the heat and set aside.

6. Save the bacon fat for the gravy. Take 2 tbsp of the fat and put it in a separate pan or use 25 grams of butter.

7. Add 25 grams of gluten-free flour and stir with a whisk until the flour is absorbed by the butter and it is a smooth mixture.

8. Cook this for 2 minutes while stirring continuously.

9. Now add a splash of broth. Gradually add stock until the gravy has the desired consistency. You probably don’t need all the stock. Taste and season with some pepper.

10. Drain the water from the potatoes and kale and mash well.

11. Add the splash of milk, mustard, pepper, salt and nutmeg.

12. Divide over two plates. Make a hole in the middle of the mashed potatoes and pour some gravy in there.

13. Serve the bacon mushroom mixture on top of the kale mashed potatoes.
