name: ✅ ❣ Gluten-free profiteroles
ingredients:
5 ml low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (0%)
5 ml water
1 pinch salt (to taste)
5 g unsalted butter  ❣ Sat fat 2.5g (13%)
5 g gluten-free flour (I use Mix C by Schär)  🟢 Fructans 5%
1/5 eggs, at room temperature  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
12 ml lactose-free whipping cream, cold  ❣ Sat fat 2.9g (14%)
1/8 package whipping cream stiffener
1/3 tsp sugar
directions:
1. Cut the butter into cubes.

2. Put the butter together with the water, the lactose-free milk and the salt in a pan. Bring this to a boil slowly. It is important that the butter has melted before the mixture starts cooking, so cut the butter into small cubes.

3. Take the pan off the heat. Add the gluten-free flour and the salt at once and stir the mixture well until all the flour is mixed in.

4. Put the pan back on medium heat. Continue to stir the dough and let it cook for about 2-3 minutes. The dough will stick to the bottom of the pan a little and will form a ball. It is important that you cook the dough for 2-3 minutes because this will help the profiteroles rise later on.

5. Put the dough into a bowl and leave it to cool for a few minutes before you continue.

6. Add the eggs one by one. Stir the dough with a wooden spoon well after adding each egg, until the egg has completely mixed in.

7. Layer a baking sheet with baking parchment and pre-heat the oven to 200°C.

8. Take a piping bag with a smooth nozzle and pipe balls of the same size onto the baking sheet. If you don’t have a piping bag, you can also do this with two teaspoons. I made about 18 medium-sized profiteroles with this batter. If you make them a little smaller, you can easily make 25.

9. Remove any peaks that are standing up on the profiteroles with a wet finger. Otherwise these will burn very quickly while baking.

10. Bake the profiteroles in the oven for 15-20 minutes. Note: never open the oven while baking the profiteroles. They will collapse if you do this. The profiteroles should have a nice golden brown colour when you take them out of the oven. If they look too light, leave them in a little longer.

11. Leave the profiteroles to cool down completely before you fill them.

12. You can also make larger profiteroles with this recipe. Make the balls of batter a little bigger and bake the profiteroles for about 10 minutes longer in the oven.

The whipping cream
13. Make sure that the whipping cream is very cold. Lactose-free whipping cream gets stiff a little more difficult than normal whipping cream, so therefore it is even more important to cool it well before whipping it.

14. Put the bowl and the whisks of your mixer in the freezer for 10 minutes before whipping the cream. If these are cold too, that can help to whip the lactose-free whipping cream stiff.

15. Put the whipping cream together with 2 tablespoons of sugar and a package of whippings cream stiffener in the cold bowl. Start to mix on a low speed and turn the speed up after a minute. Mix until the whipping cream is stiff.

16. Take a piping bag with the nozzle for filling the profiteroles and scoop the whipping cream in.

17. Make a small opening in the bottom of each profiterole with the back of a spoon.

18. Carefully fill the profiteroles with cream. In the beginning this is a bit trial and error. The first time I piped too much whipping cream into the profiterole and it came out on all sides.

19. Carefully turn your nozzle around a bit in the profiterole, so you fill the profiterole entirely and pipe carefully so you notice when the profiterole is filled with cream.

20. You can store the profiteroles in the fridge until you serve them. The gluten-free profiteroles are the nicest when they are fresh, but you can store them for about 2-3 days in the fridge.

name: ✅ ❣ Breakfast - Cinnamon Rolls
ingredients:
2 1/2 cups gluten-free 1:1 flour blend, preferably one built on rice, potato, and tapioca starches
1 tsp xanthan gum (skip if your blend already contains it)
2 1/4 tsp (1 packet) instant or rapid-rise yeast
1/4 cup white or cane sugar
1/2 tsp salt
3/4 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed), warmed to about 110F (43C) (for the dough)  ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
3 tbsp butter, melted (butter is naturally very low in lactose, so lactose-free is optional) (for the dough)  ❣ Sat fat 2.5g (13%)
1 large egg, at room temperature  ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
1 tsp vanilla extract
1/2 cup light brown or cane sugar
1 1/2 tbsp ground cinnamon
3 tbsp butter, softened (for the filling)  ❣ Sat fat 2.5g (13%)
1/2 cup cream cheese, softened (use lactose-free if you have it). Spread across 9 rolls this keeps each serving  ❣ Sat fat 2.7g (13%)
2 tbsp butter, softened (for the cream cheese glaze)  ♥ Sat fat 1.7g (9%)
3/4 cup powdered (confectioners') sugar
1 to 2 tsp low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed), to thin
directions:
Make the dough
1. Warm the lactose-free milk to about 45°C. It should feel like warm bath water, not hot. Stir in the yeast and a pinch of the sugar and let it sit for 5 minutes until foamy.

2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour blend, xanthan gum (if using), remaining sugar, and salt.

3. Pour in the yeast mixture, melted butter, egg, and vanilla. Mix with a sturdy spoon or a stand mixer until you have a soft, sticky dough. Gluten-free dough does not need kneading.

4. Cover the bowl and let the dough rise in a warm spot for 45 to 60 minutes. It will puff and soften but will not double the way wheat dough does.

Fill and shape
5. Turn the dough onto a large sheet of parchment. Place a second sheet on top and roll into a rectangle about 10 by 14 inches and a scant 1/2 inch thick.

6. Peel off the top sheet and spread the softened filling butter over the dough, leaving a 1/2 inch border along one long edge.

7. Stir the brown sugar and cinnamon together and sprinkle evenly over the butter.

8. Starting from the long edge closest to you, use the parchment to lift and roll the dough into a tight log. Pinch the seam to seal.

9. Cut into 9 even rolls with a length of unflavored dental floss or a sharp knife. Place them cut side up in a greased 8 or 9 inch pan, cover, and let rise 20 to 30 minutes.

Bake
10. Heat the oven to 175°C.

11. Bake for 22 to 28 minutes, until the tops are golden and the centers feel set.

12. Let the rolls cool in the pan for 10 minutes before glazing.

Glaze
13. Beat the cream cheese and butter until smooth, then beat in the powdered sugar and vanilla. Add lactose-free milk a teaspoon at a time until the glaze is spreadable.

14. Spread over the warm rolls and serve.

name: ✅ 💔 Low FODMAP naked cake with lemon and blueberries
ingredients:
For the cake
28 g soft butter (for the cake)  💔 Sat fat 14.3g (71%)
28 g white sugar
1/2 eggs, at room temperature  ♥ Sat fat 0.8g (4%)
1/2 tbsp low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (0%)
34 g gluten-free flour  🟢 Fructans 34%

1 pinch salt (to taste)
1 lemon (zest only)
1 tbsp for the lemon buttercream
I used this recipe from Sally’s baking addiction (but everything x 1.5)
22 g soft butter (for the lemon buttercream)  💔 Sat fat 11.2g (56%)

3/4 tsp lemon juice
3/5 tsp lactose-free heavy cream  ♥ Sat fat 1g (5%)
For the decoration
Blueberries
Strawberries

directions:
1. Pre-heat the oven to 175°C. Grease the cake tin with butter and layer with baking parchment.

2. The cake: beat the butter and the sugar together until soft and creamy. Add the eggs one by one and mix after every egg. Add the lactose-free milk and the lemon zest and mix again.

3. Put the flour, baking powder and salt together and add this to the batter little by little while you continue to mix.

4. I only had one 20 cm cake tin, so I baked the layers of the cake one after the other. It is important that the layers of the cake have the same thickness. It is best to weigh the batter, so you get equal layers. I had 2000 gram batter, so each layer was about 666 gram.

5. Pour the batter for one layer into the cake tin and level with a spatula. Bake the cake in the oven for 45-55 minutes.

6. I notice that gluten-free cake batter always darkens quickly. So I covered the cake with aluminium foil after 15 minutes of baking. It is important to check if the cake is done. Gluten-free cake usually needs some more time than normal cake and this can differ per oven. Even after 55 minutes the cake might need a few more minutes. The cake is done when a toothpick comes out clean.

7. Take the cake out of the oven. Leave to cool in the tin. Remove the cake from the tin and leave to cool completely. Repeat this for the other two layers.

8. Make sure the cakes have cooled down completely when you start decorating. Because gluten-free cake can be a bit more crumbly than normal cake, this is very important. I made the cakes the day before and I stored them in the fridge overnight. After that they were perfect to work with.

9. The frosting: Mix the soft butter for two minutes with a handmixer or in a standmixer until fluffy. Add lemon juice, cream, lemon zest, a pinch of salt and the powdered sugar little by little while you keep mixing on low speed. Continue until all ingredients are mixed well. Increase to high speed and continue to beat for another 3 minutes.

10. Assembling the cake. Make sure all layers are flat. You can use a large serrated knife to slice a thin layer off the tops of the cakes if they are not entirely flat. Place a cake layer on your turntable. Use a spatula to spread a layer of butter cream over the cake. Make a circle of blueberries around the rim of the cake. Press them slightly into the frosting to make sure you they are all even, otherwise your cake won’t be straight. Place the second layer on top of the first layer, spread the butter cream over the cake and make another circle of blueberries. Place the third layer on top. Use your spatula to spread butter cream over the top of the third layer and all around the sides of the cake. You can use a bench scraper to smoothen the sides of the cake.

11. Decorate the cake with decorations of your choice. I used strawberries, blueberries and white roses.

12. Refrigerate the cake until you serve it. If you put the cake in the fridge for more than a few hours, it is best to cover it with some plastic wrap.

name: ✅ ❣ Side - Mashed Potatoes
ingredients:
181 g Yukon Gold or russet potatoes, peeled and cut into 1 1/2-inch chunks
1/2 tsp kosher salt, for the cooking water
2/3 tbsp unsalted butter, cut into pieces  💔 Sat fat 5.1g (25%)
1/8 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed), warm  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
1/8 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
1 pinch freshly ground black pepper (to taste)
1 tsp thinly sliced chives or spring onion greens, to finish (optional)  🟢 Fructose 1%
directions:
Boil the Potatoes
1. Place the potato chunks in a large pot and cover with cold water by an inch. Add the kosher salt.

2. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to a steady simmer. Cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until a paring knife slides through a chunk with no resistance.

3. Drain in a colander. Return the hot potatoes to the empty pot and set over low heat for 30 seconds to dry them out, shaking the pan so they don't stick.

Warm the Dairy
4. While the potatoes cook, warm the milk and butter together in a small saucepan over low heat until the butter is melted and the mixture is steaming. Don't let it boil.

5. Keeping the dairy warm matters. Cold milk hitting hot potatoes seizes the starch and makes the mash gluey.

Mash and Finish
6. Mash the potatoes directly in the pot with a potato masher or ricer. A ricer gives the fluffiest texture; a masher leaves more body.

7. Pour in about three-quarters of the warm milk and butter. Fold gently with a spatula until absorbed. Add more milk a splash at a time until the mash is loose but not soupy.

8. Season with the fine salt and a few grinds of black pepper. Taste and adjust.

9. Transfer to a warm bowl and scatter the chives over the top.

name: ✅ 💔 Gluten-free stuffed speculaas
ingredients:
12 g almond flour (or almonds that you grind yourself)  🟢 Fructans 24%
12 g granulated sugar
1/2 lemon (zest only)
5/8 tsp water
1 portion egg yolk
20 g gluten-free flour  🟢 Fructans 20%
13 g dark brown sugar
3/4 tsp pumpkin spice
17 g cold butter  💔 Sat fat 8.7g (43%)
1/8 tsp baking powder
3/4 tsp low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)
1 pinch salt (to taste)
1 portion almond halves or slices (to decorate)
1 egg, to brush on top of the dough  ♥ Sat fat 1.6g (8%)
directions:
A week before
1. Mix in a bowl the almond flour with the granulated sugar. Add the lemon zest and 2-3 tablespoons water. Knead until you have a firm paste. Not too wet and not too dry.

2. Turn it into a ball and wrap the ball in clingfilm. Put it in the fridge to rest for a few days (a week is best).

Baking day
3. Mix in a bowl the gluten-free flour, dark brown sugar, pumpkin spice, salt and baking powder together. Add the cold butter and the milk and knead into a supple dough. If the dough remains too crumbly, you can add some milk. If it is too wet, you can add some extra flour.

4. Roll the dough into a ball and cover with clingfilm. Leave to rest in the fridge for at least an hour (or overnight).

5. Pre-heat the oven to 180°C Celcius (175°C). Grease a rectangular baking tin and cover with baking parchment.

6. Roll the dough into two rectangular pieces. The one piece slightly bigger than the other. If the dough is difficult to roll, you can also divide pieces of dough over the baking tin and press them with your fingers into a flat piece. Put the largest piece of dough into the baking tin and also press some dough into the sides of the tin so standing edges are formed.

7. Add an egg yolk to the ball of almond paste and knead it into a supple mixture. Divide the almond paste over the layer of dough in the baking tin.

8. Put the second layer of dough on top of the almond paste and press the sides together so the almond paste is covered by the dough on all sides.

9. Beat an egg and brush it on top of the dough. Decorate the dough with some almond halves.

10. Bake the stuffed speculaas in the oven for 30-40 minutes.

name: ✅ ❣ Sweet - Chocolate Cupcakes
ingredients:
175 g gluten-free 1:1 flour blend  🟢 Fructans 15% (15 g per serving)
1/4 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
1 cup white or cane sugar
1 tsp baking soda
1/2 tsp baking powder
1/4 tsp salt
2 large eggs, room temperature  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (1%)
1/2 cup neutral oil (or melted unsalted butter)
3/4 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed), room temperature (for the cupcakes)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (1%)
1 tsp vanilla extract
1/2 cup boiling water (or hot brewed coffee to deepen the flavor)
1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened  💔 Sat fat 5.1g (26%)
2 cups powdered (icing) sugar, sifted
2 to 3 tbsp lactose-free milk (for the cocoa buttercream)
1 portion dark chocolate shavings, capped at about 30g total across all 12 cupcakes (to finish) (optional)
directions:
Mix the batter
1. Heat the oven to 175°C and line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.

2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour blend, cocoa powder, sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt until no lumps remain.

3. Add the eggs, oil, lactose-free milk, and vanilla. Whisk until smooth.

4. Pour in the boiling water (or hot coffee) and whisk again. The batter will be thin, which is what gives these cupcakes a moist crumb.

Bake
5. Divide the batter evenly among the 12 liners, filling each about two-thirds full.

6. Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs and the tops spring back when pressed.

7. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack and cool completely before frosting.

Frost
8. Beat the softened butter until pale and creamy, about 2 minutes.

9. Add the sifted powdered sugar and cocoa powder in two additions, beating on low so it does not scatter.

10. Add the vanilla and 2 tablespoons of lactose-free milk, then beat until fluffy. Add the last tablespoon of milk only if you need a softer texture.

11. Pipe or spread onto the cooled cupcakes and finish with a few dark chocolate shavings if using.

name: ✅ 💔 Soup - Corn Chowder
ingredients:
1 cup leek, GREEN tops only, thinly sliced
3 spring onions, GREEN tops only, sliced (reserve some for garnish)  🟢 Fructose 12% (9 g per serving)
400 g potato, peeled and diced into 1cm pieces
1 tsp fresh thyme leaves
150 g fresh corn kernels, cut from 2 ears (keeps each serving at or under the 38g cap)
2 tbsp tapioca starch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water, for a thicker chowder (optional)
1 pinch grated cheddar, extra spring onion greens, cracked pepper (optional)  🟢 Fructose 0% (0.1 g per serving)
2 tbsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.9g (5%)
3 cups water or low-FODMAP chicken broth
1 cup low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.6g (3%)
1/2 cup lactose-free heavy cream  💔 Sat fat 9.9g (50%)
1/2 tsp salt, plus more to taste
1 pinch black pepper (to taste)
directions:
**Prep (bowls):**

**Large bowl — aromatics (soften):**
- Thinly slice the leek greens.
- Slice the spring onion greens (reserve some for garnish).

**Large bowl — potato (simmer):**
- Peel and dice the potato.
- Strip the thyme leaves onto this bowl.

**Medium bowl — corn (add later):**
- Cut the corn kernels from the cob.

**Small bowl — slurry (optional):**
- Mix tapioca starch with cold water if thickening.

**Medium bowl — finish:**
- Set out reserved spring onion greens, optional grated cheddar and cracked pepper.

**By the hob (no bowl):** olive oil, water or broth, lactose-free milk, cream, salt, pepper.

**1. Soften aromatics bowl:** Heat oil over medium. Soften the aromatics bowl 4–5 minutes without browning.

**2. Potato:** Stir in the potato bowl 1 minute. Add water or broth; simmer covered 12–15 minutes until potato is fork-tender.

**3. Corn:** Stir in the corn bowl; simmer uncovered about 4 minutes. Optionally blend a portion and return for creaminess.

**4. Dairy:** Lower heat; stir in milk and cream. Warm 3–4 minutes without a hard boil. Add slurry if using; simmer 1–2 minutes until coats a spoon.

**5. Finish:** Season with salt and pepper. Serve topped from the finish bowl.

Cool, portion, refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently until piping hot.

name: ✅ ♡ Low FODMAP Raisin buns
ingredients:
21 g gluten-free flour for baking bread (I used a mix that contained rice flour, teff flour, corn- and potato starch)  🟢 Fructans 21%
12 g raisins
12 ml low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (1%)
1/8 package dried yeast
2.1 g sugar
2.1 g butter, at room temperature (replace with margarine to make the recipe entirely lactose-free)  ♥ Sat fat 1.1g (5%)
1/8 egg + 1 egg for brushing the buns  ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
1/2 lemon (rind only)
1 pinch salt (to taste)
directions:
1. Soak the raisins in warm water for 15 minutes.

2. Heat the milk until it is lukewarm. Add the yeast and the sugar and stir through.

3. Put the flour into a bowl and add the milk. Knead the mixture with your hands into a supple dough.

4. Put the dough back into the bowl, cover it with a tea-towel and leave to rise in a warm place for 20 minutes.

5. Add the salt, butter, lemon rind and one egg to the dough. Knead again with your hands. Drain the raisins and dry them with a paper towel. Add them to the dough and knead again. Gluten-free dough can be very sticky in the beginning. Add some extra flour if necessary. After a while, you must be able to form the dough into a ball.

6. Put the dough back into the bowl and leave to rise in a warm place for another 20 minutes. Note that gluten-free dough won’t rise as much as normal dough. You won’t see a large difference in volume, but that doesn’t matter.

7. Cover a baking sheet with baking parchment and divide the dough into twelve pieces. Roll the pieces into balls and put them onto the baking sheet.

8. Cover the baking sheet with a tea-towel and leave the raisin buns to rise in a warm place for another 20 minutes.

9. Pre-heat the oven to 250°C.

10. Whisk the egg and brush the egg on top of the buns.

11. Bake the low FODMAP raisin buns in the oven for 15 minutes.

12. Delicious when they are still a bit warm with some butter!

13. Gluten-free bread gets dry quickly when you store it. Therefore, I advise you to eat the buns within two days after baking. Heat them in the oven for a few minutes before serving. You can also freeze the buns.

name: ✅ ❣ Breakfast - Fluffy Pancakes
ingredients:

directions:
Make the batter

2. In a large bowl, whisk together the flour blend, sugar, baking powder, salt, and xanthan gum (if using).

3. Whisk the egg, melted butter, and vanilla into the milk mixture until smooth.

4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir just until combined. A few lumps are fine. Let the batter rest for 5 to 10 minutes so the flour hydrates and the baking powder activates.

Cook the pancakes

6. Pour about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake, leaving space between them.

7. Cook until bubbles form across the surface and the edges look set, about 2 to 3 minutes. Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until golden underneath.

8. Adjust the heat down if they brown too fast. Hold finished pancakes on a plate in a 95°C oven while you cook the rest.

Serve

name: ℹ️ ❣ Low FODMAP Vegan Shepherd's Pie
ingredients:
For the lentil filling:
1 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.6g (3%)
1/16 leek (only the green parts)
1/4 size carrots, diced
1/2 tsp fresh thyme leaves (roughly chopped)
1 tsp fresh rosemary leaves (roughly chopped)
20 ml red wine
33 ml vegetable stock
25 g chopped canned tomatoes  🟢 Fructose 25%
47 g canned lentils (drain & rinse after measuring)*  🔴 Galacto-oligosaccharides 102%
30 g canned peas
1/3 bay leaves
1/6 tsp sweet paprika
8.3 g peanut butter  ♥ Sat fat 0.8g (4%)
1 pinch salt & black pepper (to taste)
For the mashed potatoes
107 g Russet potatoes
7.5 g vegan butter  ❣ Sat fat 3.8g (19%)
20 ml low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
1/6 tsp salt (plus more to taste)
1 pinch freshly cracked black pepper (to taste)
15 g vegan cheese (optionally)
33 ml veggie broth
directions:
Slice any large potatoes in half, place in a large pot, and fill with water until they’re just covered. Bring to a low boil on medium-high heat, then generously salt, cover, and cook for 20-30 minutes or until they slide off a knife very easily.

To make the lentil filling

While the potatoes are boiling start preparing the lentil filling.

Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Sauté the leeks and carrots until lightly browned and caramelized – about 5 minutes. Stir occasionally to prevent burning, but not too often so that they can brown. Add thyme and rosemary and cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent burning.

Pour in the red wine and deglaze the pan, stirring up any browned bits, until the liquid has mostly evaporated and the smell of alcohol has dissipated about 3-4 minutes. Add the vegetable broth, canned tomatoes along with bay leaves, and paprika. Stir to combine and increase the heat to bring to a boil. Once it starts to boil reduce to medium heat and add the canned lentils & the canned peas. Let it simmer until most of the liquid has been absorbed 25-30 minutes.

Turn the heat to low add the peanut butter (if using). Stir until well incorporated season with salt and pepper and set aside.

To make the mash potato topping

Once potatoes are cooked, drain, add back to the pot to evaporate any remaining water, then transfer to a mixing bowl. Use a masher, pastry cutter or large fork to mash until smooth. Add vegan butter and season with salt and pepper to taste.

Assemble & Bake

Transfer the lentil filling into an oven safe dish, then, spoon and carefully spread out the Mashed Potato Topping on top, covering the whole surface. For more flavour, drizzle the top with olive oil or vegan parmesan cheese.

Bake for 20 minutes, or until the lentil filling starts to bubble up. Remove from the oven and turn on your oven’s broiler. Place the pan under the broiler for a few minutes until the crust is golden brown. To finish, drizzle with more olive oil and garnish with fresh parsley, if desired.

Store any leftovers in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. You can also freeze them for up to 3 months.

name: ℹ️ 💔 Side - Green Bean Casserole
ingredients:
76 g fresh green beans, trimmed and cut into 2-inch pieces
3/8 tsp kosher salt, for the blanching water
3/4 tsp unsalted butter  ♥ Sat fat 1.9g (10%)
3/4 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.5g (2%)
1 tsp gluten-free all-purpose flour  🟢 Fructans 3%
1/8 cup low-FODMAP chicken broth
1 1/2 tbsp heavy cream  🟡 Lactose 56%  💔 Sat fat 7.4g (37%)
1 1/2 tbsp low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)  ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
1/8 tsp fine salt, plus more to taste
1/8 tsp freshly ground black pepper
0.03 tsp freshly grated nutmeg
1/4 tsp soy sauce or tamari (gluten-free)
1/8 leeks, green tops only, cut into thin matchsticks
1/8 cup gluten-free panko or plain gluten-free breadcrumbs
1/3 tbsp finely grated Parmesan  ♥ Sat fat 0.8g (4%)
1 pinch fine salt (for the crispy leek-green topping)
directions:
Blanch the Green Beans
1. Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and add the kosher salt. Set a large bowl of ice water next to the stove.

2. Drop the green beans into the boiling water and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until bright green and just tender.

3. Drain and transfer immediately to the ice bath. Once cool, drain again and pat dry with a clean towel. Set aside.

Make the Cream Sauce
4. Melt the butter with the olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat.

5. Whisk in the gluten-free flour and cook, whisking constantly, for 90 seconds. The roux should smell toasty and turn a shade darker.

6. Pour in the chicken broth in a slow stream, whisking until smooth. Add the heavy cream and lactose-free milk the same way.

7. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, whisking often, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

8. Stir in the salt, pepper, nutmeg, and soy sauce. Taste and adjust. Pull off the heat.

Crisp the Leek Greens
9. Heat the olive oil in a wide skillet over medium heat.

10. Add the leek-green matchsticks and cook, stirring often, for 6 to 8 minutes, until deeply golden and crisp at the edges. Watch them in the last two minutes; they go from golden to burnt fast.

11. Transfer to a paper-towel-lined plate and season with a pinch of salt.

12. In a small bowl, toss the breadcrumbs, Parmesan, and 1/4 teaspoon salt together. Fold in half the crispy leek greens; reserve the rest for the top.

Assemble and Bake
13. Heat the oven to 190°C. Butter a 3-quart (9x13-inch) baking dish.

14. Combine the blanched green beans and cream sauce in the baking dish and stir to coat every piece.

15. Scatter the breadcrumb-Parmesan mixture evenly over the top.

16. Bake for 20 minutes, until the sauce is bubbling at the edges and the topping is golden.

17. Scatter the reserved crispy leek greens over the hot casserole and serve.

name: ✅ ❣ Low FODMAP & gluten free lemon meringue pie
ingredients:
For the sweet pastry:
180g gluten free plain flour  🟢 Fructans 18% (18 g per serving)
20g ground almonds
1 teaspoon xanthan gum
1/2 teaspoon fine sea salt
100g unsalted butter  💔 Sat fat 5.1g (25%)
1 1/2 tablespoons icing sugar
1 medium egg  ♥ Sat fat 0.2g (1%)
1 teaspoon vanilla extract
1-2 tablespoons low FODMAP milk (unsweetened almond, soy-protein soy or lactose-free semi-skimmed)
For the filling:
5 tablespoons cornflour
250g caster sugar
1/2 teaspoon sea salt
310ml water
1/2 juice and zest of 3 lemons (you’re after about 100ml lemon juice) (optional)
5 free-range medium egg yolks  ♥ Sat fat 0.8g (4%)
40g unsalted butter, cold  ❣ Sat fat 2g (10%)
For the meringue:
75ml water
5 free-range medium egg whites  ♥ Sat fat 0.8g (4%)
directions:
1. Start the pastry the day before. Add the gluten free flour, ground almonds, xanthan gum and salt into a bowl and stir with a fork to combine. Add the butter to the flour mixture and rub in with your fingertips until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs. Alternatively, use a food processor and pulse the ingredients to reach this stage (I find this so much easier as I have hot hands!) Sift over the sugar and stir it in. If you’re using a food processor, tip the ingredients out into a large bowl.

2. Whisk the egg and vanilla extract together and stir the liquid into the flour mixture, little by little, distributing it as quickly as possible with a cutlery knife. You might not need all of the liquid, so see how you go. If you need any more, add a teaspoon of milk at a time. Use the flat of the knife to bring the dough together, then pull the pastry together with your hands, tip out onto cling film and shape into a disc, touching the dough as little as possible, but making sure the dough is smooth and there are no cracks. Wrap tightly and chill in the fridge overnight.

3. When you’re ready to bake the pastry, preheat your oven to 200C/180C fan/gas mark 6 and have ready a 23cm/9inch loose-bottomed fluted tart tin. Roll out your pastry onto a clean, floured surface, to the thickness of a pound coin. Using your rolling pin, lift up the pastry and place it over the tart tin, pushing the pastry into the edges. Cut off any excess, leaving a small overhang and place the pastry in the fridge for 30 minutes to firm up.

4. When chilled, use a sharp knife or the rolling pin to trim the pastry to the edges of the tin. Prick the base of the pastry all over with a fork, then line the pastry with scrunched and un-scrunched greaseproof paper and fill with baking beans. Blind bake for 20 minutes, then remove the paper and baking beans and bake the tart case for another 5-10 minutes, or until the pastry is golden, sandy to the touch and has no grey patches. Turn the oven off and leave the tart case to cool.

5. To make the lemon curd filling, add the cornflour, sugar, salt, water and lemon juice and zest (if using) to a medium saucepan and whisk to combine. Add the egg yolks and whisk again. Place the saucepan over a medium heat and cook the mixture for about 6-7 minutes, stirring all the time. Once the mixture starts to thicken and bubble, cook for another couple of minutes (this ensures the cornflour does its setting thing) and then remove from the heat. Whisk in the cold butter, allow to cool for a few minutes and then pour the filling into your cooled tart case. Allow the filling to cool to room temp, before placing the pie in the fridge for at least a couple of hours, or until fully chilled and set.

6. To make the meringue, place the sugar and water in a small saucepan over a medium heat. Rest a sugar thermometer on the side of the pan, so that it’s touching the liquid and then bring the sugar to 120C. Meanwhile, add the egg whites to a large bowl and whisk to soft peaks. Once the sugar reaches 120C, slowly pour it into the egg whites, continuing to whisk all the time. Turn the whisk up to high and whisk the meringue until it’s cooled to room temperature.

7. To finish the pie, dollop the meringue on top of the lemon curd, carefully pushing it down, right to the edges. Swoosh with the back of a spoon or palette knife any way you like, then with a blowtorch (or under a hot grill) lightly caramelise the edges before serving. Before the meringue is added, the pie can be made 2 days ahead and kept chilled in the fridge.

7. Place the dish in the oven and bake for 20 minutes, then add a few sage leaves on top, a drizzle of olive oil and bake for another 20. 4. Pat the chicken dry with paper towels. If using breasts, slice thick ones in half horizontally so they cook evenly.

5. Place the chicken in a zip-top bag or shallow dish and pour the marinade over it. Turn to coat every piece.

6. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes and up to 12 hours. Because the marinade is acidic, do not go past 24 hours or the surface can turn mushy.

Cook and rest
7. Cook the chicken by your preferred method: grill or pan-sear over medium-high for about 5 to 6 minutes per side, or bake at 220°C for 18 to 22 minutes.

8. Cook until the thickest part reaches 75°C on an instant-read thermometer. Discard any leftover raw marinade; do not reuse it as a sauce.

9. Rest the chicken 5 minutes before slicing so the juices settle.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Thai Trio – Thai Green, Thai Red & Massaman Sauces
ingredients:
For the Thai Green Curry Sauce:
90 g light coconut milk  🟢 Sorbitol 25% (15 g per serving)  ♥ Sat fat 1.1g (5%)
40 ml water
35 g bamboo shoots (tinned, drained)
28 g green pepper, sliced  🟢 Fructans 6% (4.7 g per serving)
22 g red pepper, sliced  🟢 Fructose 9% (3.7 g per serving)
8 g fresh coriander, stalks and leaves
4 g lemongrass (about 1/2 stalk, tender inner part), finely chopped
4 g green chilli (about 1), deseeded for less heat
4 g fresh ginger (about 2 tsp grated)
1 tsp tamari or gluten-free soy sauce
1 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (1%)
1 tbsp tapioca starch, mixed with 1 tbsp of the water
1/2 tbsp lime juice
1/2 tsp caster sugar
1/4 tsp salt
1/4 tsp cumin seeds
1 kaffir lime leaf
For the Thai Massaman Sauce:
130 ml water
90 g light coconut milk  🟢 Sorbitol 25% (15 g per serving)  ♥ Sat fat 1.1g (5%)
8 g lemongrass (about 1 stalk, tender inner part), finely chopped
7 g fresh ginger (about 1 tbsp grated)
4 tsp tapioca starch, mixed with 1 tbsp of the water
4 g fresh coriander, stalks and leaves
2/3 tsp coriander seeds
1/3 tsp cumin seeds
1 pinch cayenne pepper
1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
3 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed
1/8 tsp ground turmeric
1 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (1%)
1/2 tsp salt
1/2 tsp lime juice
1/3 tsp caster sugar
2 kaffir lime leaves
For the Thai Red Curry Sauce:
95 g light coconut milk  🟢 Sorbitol 26% (16 g per serving)  ♥ Sat fat 1.1g (6%)
60 ml water
50 g red pepper, sliced  🟢 Fructose 19% (8.3 g per serving)
9 g red chillies (about 2), deseeded for less heat
7 g lemongrass (about 1 stalk, tender inner part), finely chopped
4 tsp tapioca starch, mixed with 1 tbsp of the water
6 g fresh ginger (about 1 tbsp grated)
1 tsp tamari or gluten-free soy sauce
1 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.1g (1%)
1/2 tsp salt
1 tsp cumin seeds
1/2 tsp lime juice
2 g fresh coriander, chopped
1/2 tsp caster sugar
3 kaffir lime leaves
1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
directions:
1. **Shared prep (do once for all the sauces):**
- Peel and finely grate all the ginger in one go: 17 g in total (Thai Green 4 g, Massaman 7 g, Thai Red 6 g).
- Trim the lemongrass to the tender inner part and chop it all: 19 g in total (Thai Green 4 g, Massaman 8 g, Thai Red 7 g).
- Wash the coriander; chop the stalks and leaves separately (stalks go in the pastes, leaves at the end): 14 g in total (Thai Green 8 g, Massaman 4 g, Thai Red 2 g).
- Dice or slice all the green pepper: 28 g (Thai Green).
- Dice or slice all the red pepper: 72 g in total (Thai Green 22 g, Thai Red 50 g).
- Deseed and chop the red chillies: 9 g (Thai Red).
- Deseed and chop the green chilli: 4 g (Thai Green).
- Squeeze the lime juice: 2 1/2 tsp in total (Thai Green 1 1/2 tsp, Massaman 1/2 tsp, Thai Red 1/2 tsp).
- Toast the whole seeds in one dry pan, 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind: the cumin seeds can be toasted and ground in bulk and then measured out per sauce; toast Massaman's coriander seeds separately.
- Blitz the curry pastes one after another in the same mini chopper (Thai Green, Massaman, Thai Red), mildest first, each with 1 tbsp of its own water.
- Mix each sauce's tapioca starch with its own measured water in a small cup and label it.
- Open one tin of light coconut milk for the group (275 g needed); stir it well first.

2. **Thai Green Curry Sauce** (use its share of the shared prep):
- Dry-toast the cumin seeds for 1 minute, then grind.
- Blitz or pound the coriander stalks, lemongrass, green chilli and ginger with 1 tbsp of the water to a green paste (no oil).
- Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat and fry the paste with the cumin for 2 minutes until fragrant.
- Add the rest of the water, the light coconut milk, lime leaf, tamari, sugar and salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
- Add the bamboo shoots and peppers and simmer for 4-5 minutes. Stir in the tapioca starch mixed with water and simmer for 1 minute.
- Finish with the lime juice and coriander leaves; remove the lime leaf.

3. **Thai Massaman Sauce** (use its share of the shared prep):
- Dry-toast the coriander and cumin seeds for 1-2 minutes, then grind.
- Blitz or pound the lemongrass, ginger and coriander stalks with 1 tbsp of the water to a paste (no oil).
- Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat and fry the paste for 2 minutes, then add the ground seeds, cayenne and turmeric for 30 seconds.
- Add the rest of the water, cinnamon, cardamom, lime leaves, salt and sugar (these infuse in the liquid). Simmer for 10 minutes; remove the cardamom pods and lime leaves.
- Stir in the light coconut milk and the tapioca starch mixed with water; simmer gently for 2 minutes. Finish with the lime juice and coriander leaves.

4. **Thai Red Curry Sauce** (use its share of the shared prep):
- Dry-toast the cumin seeds for 1 minute, then grind.
- Blitz or pound the red chillies, lemongrass and ginger with 1 tbsp of the water to a red paste (no oil).
- Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat and fry the paste with the cumin and cayenne for 2 minutes until fragrant.
- Add the rest of the water, the light coconut milk, lime leaves, tamari, sugar and salt and bring to a gentle simmer.
- Add the red pepper and simmer for 4-5 minutes. Stir in the tapioca starch mixed with water and simmer for 1 minute.
- Finish with the lime juice and coriander; remove the lime leaves.

5. Cool, then split each sauce into single portions and freeze, labelled with the sauce and date: Thai Green 130 g, Massaman 125 g, Thai Red 130 g.
notes: Cook-together recipe for the Bay's Kitchen Thai trio: Bay's Kitchen Thai Green Curry Sauce, Bay's Kitchen Thai Massaman Sauce, Bay's Kitchen Thai Red Curry Sauce. Each sauce's amounts are exactly its own recipe (2 single portions each), so the shopping list and scaling work as usual; the saving is in the shared prep and one shop. The single-sauce recipes are unchanged. See docs/bays-kitchen-batch-plan.md for the overlap between the sauces.

ingredients:

For the Tikka Masala Sauce:
95 g tinned chopped tomatoes  🟢 Fructose 16% (16 g per serving)
80 ml water
30 g light coconut milk  🟢 Sorbitol 8% (5 g per serving)  ♥ Sat fat 0.4g (2%)
1 tbsp tomato purée  🟢 Fructose 4% (2.5 g per serving)

directions:
1. **Shared prep (do once for all the sauces):**
- Peel and finely grate all the ginger in one go: 24 g in total (Korma 15 g, Katsu 7 g, Tikka 2 g).
- Wash and chop the coriander: 4 g (Tikka).
- Squeeze the lemon juice: 1 1/2 tbsp in total (Korma 1/2 tsp, Katsu 2 tsp, Tikka 2 tsp).
- Toast the whole seeds in one dry pan, 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind: the cumin seeds, coriander seeds can be toasted and ground in bulk and then measured out per sauce; toast Katsu's fenugreek seeds, fennel seeds, mustard seeds separately (fenugreek turns bitter past golden, so watch it).
- Mix each sauce's tapioca starch with its own measured water in a small cup and label it.
- Open one tin of light coconut milk for the group (200 g needed); stir it well first.
- Open one tin of chopped tomatoes (125 g needed).

2. **Korma Curry Sauce** (use its share of the shared prep):
- Dry-toast the coriander and cumin seeds for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind (this replaces the garam masala blend).
- Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat. Add the ginger for 1 minute, then the ground seeds and turmeric for 30 seconds, adding a splash of water if they catch.
- Add the tomatoes, water, sugar, salt, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom (these infuse in the liquid, no frying needed). Simmer for 10 minutes, then fish out the cloves and cardamom pods.
- Stir in the light coconut milk and the tapioca starch mixed with water; simmer gently for 2 minutes until creamy. Do not boil hard.
- Finish with the lemon juice and black pepper.

3. **Katsu Curry Sauce** (use its share of the shared prep):
- Dry-toast the coriander, fenugreek, cumin, fennel and mustard seeds for 1-2 minutes until fragrant (fenugreek turns bitter if it goes past golden), then grind. This replaces the curry powder.
- Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat. Add the ginger for 30 seconds, then the ground seeds, turmeric and chilli powder for 30 seconds, adding a splash of water if they catch.
- Add the water, tamari and sugar and simmer for 5 minutes.
- Stir in the light coconut milk and the tapioca starch mixed with water; simmer for 2 minutes until thick and glossy. For the classic smooth katsu sauce, blend.
- Finish with the lemon juice and black pepper.

4. **Tikka Masala Sauce** (use its share of the shared prep):
- Dry-toast the cumin and coriander seeds in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind.
- Warm the olive oil over a medium-low heat. Add the ginger for 30 seconds, then the ground seeds, paprika, turmeric and chilli and stir for 30-45 seconds, adding a splash of the water if they catch.
- Add the tomatoes, tomato purée, the rest of the water, sugar and salt. Simmer for 15 minutes.
- Stir in the light coconut milk and the tapioca starch mixed with water; simmer for 1-2 minutes until thickened.
- Finish with the lemon juice, fresh coriander and black pepper.

5. Cool, then split each sauce into single portions and freeze, labelled with the sauce and date: Korma 130 g, Katsu 135 g, Tikka 125 g.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Thai Trio – Thai Green, Thai Red & Massaman Sauces
ingredients:
275 g light coconut milk  🟠 Sorbitol 76% (46 g per serving)  ❣ Sat fat 3.2g (16%)
35 g bamboo shoots (tinned)

1 1/3 tsp caster sugar
1 tbsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
2 tsp tamari (or gluten-free soy sauce)
2 1/2 tsp lime juice
17 g fresh ginger (peeled)
19 g lemongrass (tender inner part)
14 g fresh coriander (stalks and leaves)
4 g green chilli (deseeded for less heat)
9 g red chillies (deseeded for less heat)
28 g green pepper  🟢 Fructans 6% (4.7 g per serving)
72 g red pepper  🟢 Fructose 28% (12 g per serving)
6 kaffir lime leaves
about 1 1/2 tsp cumin seeds
2/3 tsp coriander seeds
3 green cardamom pods (lightly crushed)

directions:
1. **Shared prep, for all the sauces:**
- Open the light coconut milk and stir it well (275 g).
- Squeeze all the lime juice (2 1/2 tsp).
- Peel and finely grate all the ginger (17 g).
- Trim all the lemongrass to the tender inner part and chop it finely (19 g).
- Wash all the coriander (14 g); chop the stalks and the leaves separately.

- Squeeze all the lime juice.
- Peel and finely grate all the ginger.
- Trim all the lemongrass to the tender inner part and chop it finely.
- Wash all the coriander; chop the stalks and the leaves separately.
- Dry-toast all the cumin seeds together in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind.
- Toast and grind separately, the same way: the Massaman coriander seeds.

2. **Fill the bowls.** Weigh each sauce's share of the shared prep, and its own ingredients from its list, into its named bowls:

**Thai Green:**
- Green oil: 34% of the olive oil
- Green water: the water
- Green paste: the stalks from 57% of the fresh coriander, 21% of the lemongrass, the green chilli, 24% of the fresh ginger
- Green spice: 16% of the ground cumin seeds
- Green liquid: 33% of the light coconut milk, 17% of the kaffir lime leaves, the tamari, 38% of the caster sugar, the salt
- Green veg: the bamboo shoots, the green pepper, the red pepper
- Green thickener: 27% of the tapioca starch
- Green finish: 60% of the lime juice, the leaves from 57% of the fresh coriander

**Thai Red:**
- Red oil: 33% of the olive oil
- Red water: the water
- Red paste: the red chillies, 37% of the lemongrass, 35% of the fresh ginger
- Red spice: 63% of the ground cumin seeds, the cayenne pepper

- Massaman water: the water
- Massaman paste: 42% of the lemongrass, 41% of the fresh ginger, the stalks from 29% of the fresh coriander
- Massaman spice: 21% of the ground cumin seeds, the ground coriander seeds, the cayenne pepper, the ground turmeric
- Massaman infusion: the ground cinnamon, the green cardamom pods, 33% of the kaffir lime leaves, the salt, 25% of the caster sugar

- Massaman finish: 20% of the lime juice, the leaves from 29% of the fresh coriander

- Blitz or pound the **Green paste** with a splash from the **Green water** to a paste (no oil).
- Warm the **Green oil** over a medium-low heat and fry the paste with the **Green spice** for 2 minutes until fragrant.
- Add the rest of the **Green water** and the **Green liquid** and bring to a gentle simmer.
- Add the **Green veg** and simmer for 4-5 minutes. Mix the **Green thickener** with a splash of cold water, stir it in and simmer for 1 minute.

- Add the **Red veg** and simmer for 4-5 minutes. Mix the **Red thickener** with a splash of cold water, stir it in and simmer for 1 minute.

- Katsu oil: 33% of the olive oil
- Katsu water: the water
- Katsu ginger: 29% of the fresh ginger
- Katsu spice: 14% of the ground cumin seeds, 28% of the ground coriander seeds, the ground fenugreek seeds, the ground fennel seeds, the ground mustard seeds, 32% of the ground turmeric, the mild chilli powder

- Stir in the **Tikka finish**.

- Blitz or pound the **paste bowl** with a splash from the **jug** to a paste (no oil).
- Warm the **oil** over a medium-low heat and fry the paste with the **spice bowl** for 2 minutes until fragrant.
- Add the rest of the water from the **jug** and the **liquid bowl** and bring to a gentle simmer.
- Add the **veg bowl** and simmer for 4-5 minutes. Mix the **thickener** with a splash of cold water, stir it in and simmer for 1 minute.
- Stir in the **finish bowl**; remove the lime leaves.

5. **Thai Massaman Sauce**
Single recipe: [recipe:ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Thai Massaman Sauce]
- Blitz or pound the **paste bowl** with a splash from the **jug** to a paste (no oil).
- Warm the **oil** over a medium-low heat and fry the paste for 2 minutes, then add the **spice bowl** for 30 seconds.
- Add the rest of the water from the **jug** and the **infusion bowl** (these infuse in the liquid). Simmer for 10 minutes; remove the cardamom pods and lime leaves.
- Whisk the **cream bowl** (the tapioca starch stirred into the coconut milk), stir it in and simmer gently for 2 minutes.
- Stir in the **finish bowl**.

6. Cool, then split each sauce into single portions and freeze, labelled with the sauce and date: Thai Green 130 g, Thai Red 130 g, Massaman 125 g.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Indian Trio – Korma, Tikka Masala & Katsu Sauces
ingredients:
Shared (all the sauces):
200 g light coconut milk  🟡 Sorbitol 56% (33 g per serving)  ❣ Sat fat 2.3g (12%)
1 1/2 tbsp lemon juice
24 g fresh ginger (peeled)
2 1/3 tsp cumin seeds
1 1/4 tbsp coriander seeds (about)
1 tbsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
2 1/3 tsp ground turmeric
275 ml water
2 tbsp caster sugar
5 1/3 tbsp tapioca starch
3 pinches black pepper
Korma Curry Sauce:
30 g tinned chopped tomatoes  🟢 Fructose 5% (5 g per serving)
1/2 tsp salt
1/4 tsp ground cinnamon
2 whole cloves
4 green cardamom pods (lightly crushed)
Katsu Curry Sauce:
1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds
1/4 tsp fennel seeds
1/8 tsp mustard seeds
1/4 tsp mild chilli powder
1 1/2 tbsp tamari (or gluten-free soy sauce)
Tikka Masala Sauce:
2/3 tsp sweet paprika
1 pinch dried chilli flakes
95 g tinned chopped tomatoes  🟢 Fructose 16% (16 g per serving)
1 tbsp tomato purée  🟢 Fructose 4% (2.5 g per serving)
1/3 tsp salt
4 g fresh coriander (stalks and leaves)
directions:
1. **Shared prep, for all the sauces:**
- Open the light coconut milk and stir it well.
- Squeeze all the lemon juice.
- Peel and finely grate all the ginger.
- Dry-toast all the cumin seeds and coriander seeds together in a dry pan for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, then grind.
- Toast and grind separately, the same way: the Katsu fenugreek seeds and fennel seeds and mustard seeds. Fenugreek turns bitter if it goes past golden.

2. **Fill the bowls.** Weigh each sauce's share of the shared prep (the percentages) and its own ingredients ("its …", from its section of the ingredient list) into its bowls:

**Korma:**
- Oil: 34% of the olive oil
- Jug: 31% of the water
- Ginger: 63% of the fresh ginger
- Spice bowl: 22% of the ground cumin seeds, 29% of the ground coriander seeds, 54% of the ground turmeric
- Simmer bowl: its tinned chopped tomatoes, 42% of the caster sugar, its salt, its ground cinnamon, its whole cloves, its green cardamom pods
- Cream bowl: 45% of the light coconut milk, 38% of the tapioca starch
- Finish bowl: 11% of the lemon juice, 34% of the black pepper

**Katsu:**
- Oil: 33% of the olive oil
- Jug: 40% of the water
- Ginger: 29% of the fresh ginger
- Spice bowl: 14% of the ground cumin seeds, 28% of the ground coriander seeds, its ground fenugreek seeds, its ground fennel seeds, its ground mustard seeds, 32% of the ground turmeric, its mild chilli powder
- Simmer bowl: its tamari, 50% of the caster sugar
- Cream bowl: 40% of the light coconut milk, 37% of the tapioca starch
- Finish bowl: 45% of the lemon juice, 33% of the black pepper

**Tikka:**
- Oil: 33% of the olive oil
- Jug: 29% of the water
- Ginger: 8% of the fresh ginger
- Spice bowl: 64% of the ground cumin seeds, 43% of the ground coriander seeds, its sweet paprika, 14% of the ground turmeric, its dried chilli flakes
- Simmer bowl: its tinned chopped tomatoes, its tomato purée, 8% of the caster sugar, its salt
- Cream bowl: 15% of the light coconut milk, 25% of the tapioca starch
- Finish bowl: 44% of the lemon juice, its fresh coriander, 33% of the black pepper

3. **Korma Curry Sauce**
Single recipe: [recipe:ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Korma Curry Sauce]
- Warm the **oil** over a medium-low heat. Add the **ginger** for 1 minute, then the **spice bowl** for 30 seconds, adding a splash from the **jug** if they catch.
- Add the rest of the water from the **jug** and the **simmer bowl** (these infuse in the liquid, no frying needed). Simmer for 10 minutes, then fish out the cloves and cardamom pods.
- Whisk the **cream bowl** (the tapioca starch stirred into the coconut milk), stir it in and simmer gently for 2 minutes until creamy. Do not boil hard.
- Stir in the **finish bowl**.

4. **Katsu Curry Sauce**
Single recipe: [recipe:ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Katsu Curry Sauce]
- Warm the **oil** over a medium-low heat. Add the **ginger** for 30 seconds, then the **spice bowl** for 30 seconds, adding a splash from the **jug** if they catch.
- Add the rest of the water from the **jug** and the **simmer bowl** and simmer for 5 minutes.
- Whisk the **cream bowl** (the tapioca starch stirred into the coconut milk), stir it in and simmer for 2 minutes until thick and glossy. For the classic smooth katsu sauce, blend.
- Stir in the **finish bowl**.

5. **Tikka Masala Sauce**
Single recipe: [recipe:ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Tikka Masala Sauce]
- Warm the **oil** over a medium-low heat. Add the **ginger** for 30 seconds, then the **spice bowl** and stir for 30-45 seconds, adding a splash from the **jug** if they catch.
- Add the rest of the water from the **jug** and the **simmer bowl**. Simmer for 15 minutes.
- Whisk the **cream bowl** (the tapioca starch stirred into the coconut milk), stir it in and simmer for 1-2 minutes until thickened.
- Stir in the **finish bowl**.

6. Cool, then split each sauce into single portions and freeze, labelled with the sauce and date: Korma 130 g, Katsu 135 g, Tikka 125 g.

The ingredient list is the combined shop (an equal number of single portions of each sauce); step 1 preps what all the sauces share and splits it per sauce, then each sauce adds its own ingredients. The single-sauce recipes are unchanged. See docs/bays-kitchen-batch-plan.md for the overlaps.

name: ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Tomato Pair – Tomato & Basil and Spicy Arrabbiata Sauces
ingredients:
Shared (all the sauces):
330 g tinned chopped tomatoes  🟠 Fructose 82% (82 g per serving)
3/4 tsp lemon juice
2 tsp olive oil  ♥ Sat fat 0.3g (2%)
3 tbsp tomato purée  🟢 Fructose 17% (11 g per serving)
105 ml water
1 tsp caster sugar
1/2 tsp salt
2 tbsp tapioca starch (optional, or simmer 10 minutes longer)
2 pinches black pepper
Tomato & Basil Sauce:
1 tsp balsamic vinegar
1/2 tsp dried oregano
1 tbsp chives
3 g fresh basil
Spicy Arrabbiata Sauce:
1/4 tsp cayenne pepper
1 pinch dried chilli flakes
5 g sundried tomatoes (dry-packed)  🟢 Fructose 10% (1.2 g per serving)
directions:
1. **Shared prep, for all the sauces:**
- Open the tinned chopped tomatoes.
- Squeeze all the lemon juice.

2. **Fill the bowls.** Weigh each sauce's share of the shared prep (the percentages) and its own ingredients ("its …", from its section of the ingredient list) into its bowls:

**Tom & Basil:**
- Oil: 50% of the olive oil
- Jug: 62% of the water
- Simmer bowl: 42% of the tinned chopped tomatoes, 67% of the tomato purée, its balsamic vinegar, its dried oregano, 50% of the caster sugar, 50% of the salt
- Thickener: 50% of the tapioca starch (optional)
- Finish bowl: its chives, its fresh basil, 67% of the lemon juice, 50% of the black pepper

**Arrabbiata:**
- Oil: 50% of the olive oil
- Jug: 38% of the water
- Chilli bowl: its cayenne pepper, its dried chilli flakes
- Simmer bowl: 58% of the tinned chopped tomatoes, 33% of the tomato purée, its sundried tomatoes, 50% of the caster sugar, 50% of the salt
- Thickener: 50% of the tapioca starch (optional)
- Finish bowl: 33% of the lemon juice, 50% of the black pepper

3. **Tomato & Basil Sauce**
Single recipe: [recipe:ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Tomato & Basil Sauce]
- Warm the **oil** in a small pan over a medium-low heat.
- Add the water from the **jug** and the **simmer bowl**. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.
- For a thicker sauce, mix the **thickener** with a splash of cold water, stir it in and simmer for 1 minute (or simmer 10 minutes longer instead).
- Off the heat, stir in the **finish bowl**. Taste for salt.

4. **Spicy Arrabbiata Sauce**
Single recipe: [recipe:ℹ️ ♡ Bay's Kitchen Spicy Arrabbiata Sauce]
- Warm the **oil** over a medium-low heat, add the **chilli bowl** and stir for 20-30 seconds (chilli heat is fat-soluble, so this is the step that needs the oil).
- Add the water from the **jug** and the **simmer bowl**. Simmer for 15-20 minutes until slightly thickened.
- For a thicker sauce, mix the **thickener** with a splash of cold water, stir it in and simmer for 1 minute.
- Stir in the **finish bowl**.

5. Cool, then split each sauce into single portions and freeze, labelled with the sauce and date: Tom & Basil 125 g, Arrabbiata 120 g.
